tasks.outcome:
Prefix each Tasks row title with the task key (`FM3K-12`), inline and dim mono, the same way a task-bound Activity line leads with its key. Keep the project name in the trailing slot. Do not use the opaque record id.

What is there now. Tasks is the now panel (`src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/now/`). `row()` in `now.frame.js` paints a status dot, then `span.title` set to `task.title` (plus one dim word, ` · blocked` or ` · held`), then `span.key` set to the project display name. The key is only on the hover title (`${task.key} · ${task.title}`), the filter (key or title), and `data-now-key`. `now.html` ellipsizes `.title` as one line and gives the trailing `.key` mono `--text-xs` / `--fg-3`, with `fit-content(40%)` so the name does not crush the title. The design skill says the same: `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.prompt.md` and `NowPanel.jsx` `NowRow` (title text, then project name). `now.frame.test.ts` pins it: a row whose key is `FI3-12` and title is `Ship the row chrome` paints chrome `firstmate-3000`, and the chrome must not contain `FI3-12`.

Activity is the left-rail feed (`activity.frame.js` `row()`, styles in `activity.html`). A line with `taskKey` puts a `span.key` (`data-feed-key`) before the text, then a space, inside `.line`, which ellipsizes as a whole. The key is `font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--fg-3)`. Age stays in its own column. Only some lines get the prefix: `src/shared/feed.ts` sets `taskKey` from `event.key` on task timeline lines; captain turns, notes, and project lines have none. `tests/e2e/task-protocol.spec.ts` reads `[data-feed-key]` as `SCR-1` beside `.text`, not inside it. `src/shared/tasks.ts` documents `key` as `<PROJECT_KEY>-<seq>`, the conversational handle; `id` is the opaque record id (`data-now-row`). Activity prefixes the key, never the id.

How to do it. In `now.frame.js` `row()`, inside `span.title`, before the title text and before the optional word: a span with its own class (not `.key`), `data-now-title-key`, text `task.key`, then a space, then the title. Every Tasks row has a key, so every row gets the prefix. CSS in `now.html`, copied from Activity's `.key` and nothing else: mono, `--text-xs`, `--fg-3`, and `flex-shrink: 0` is unnecessary if it stays an inline span inside the already-ellipsizing `.title` (the key stays at the start; the title clips from the end). Do not reuse class `key`: that class is the trailing project cell (ellipsis, `min-width: 0`) and brightens to `--fg-2` when the row is selected. A prefix with that class would shrink on its own and change color on selection. Leave the trailing project name, the hover title, the filter, and `data-now-key` as they are.

Do not put the key in its own grid column, and do not replace the project name with the key. Activity prefixes the text and keeps the age; Tasks should prefix the title and keep the project name. That also keeps the existing chrome assertion true.

The frame test's fake `append` only accepts elements and does not fold children into `textContent`. Match Activity's real-DOM `append(keySpan, " ", text)` only if the fake learns to accept a text node; otherwise put the title in its own span. Update `paintedRows` to read the prefix span separately and assert `FI3-12` then `Ship the row chrome`, with chrome still `firstmate-3000`.

Stale copy to update in the same change, skill first: `NowPanel.prompt.md`, `NowPanel.jsx` `NowRow`, the row comment in `now.html`, and the sentence in `docs/ui-plugins.md` that the key stays only on hover, search, and the locator. Leave the generic `Row` primitive and personal-panel examples alone; those still trail one datum and are not the Tasks panel. Collapsed Tasks chrome is counts only (`NowCompact.tsx`) and needs no prefix.

No captain decision. The visible id is the key, because that is what Activity already prints.

tasks.outcome:
The firstmate-3000-local password dialog is the install step, not a Claude sign-in. Cancel it. The password is not the Mac login password.

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile runs scripts/prepare-local-codesign.mjs from postinstall. That always calls ensureKeychain, which runs security set-keychain-settings on ~/.firstmate-3000/local-codesign/firstmate-3000-local.keychain-db before unlock-keychain -p. set-keychain-settings has no password flag, so a locked keychain (normal after sleep or restart) opens SecurityAgent. FI3-7 recorded that call and macOS answering “User canceled the operation.” predev and tests/local-codesign.test.ts hit the same function. The random password is in ~/.firstmate-3000/local-codesign/secret.

Do not pass -u to unlock-keychain. On this Mac, security help unlock-keychain defines -u as “Prompt for the password via GUI.”

Remedy, without regenerating the certificate (that would re-ask for the Claude sign-in): routine install, dev, and verify must not call security at all when designated-requirement.txt exists and codesign --verify --strict -R passes on the dev Electron app. That check does not use the private key. Only when a signature is actually missing (codesign:local, package:mac, or that check failing): call set-keychain-settings only immediately after create-keychain -p, never on an existing keychain; unlock with unlock-keychain -p and never -u, and stop if that fails; sign with codesign --keychain pointing at that file; stop adding the keychain to the user search list (codesign(1) says --keychain limits identity lookup to that file). Once, rewrite the user search list to drop firstmate-3000-local.keychain-db, refusing an empty read, so git does not keep prompting: this project's origin is HTTPS and credential.helper is osxkeychain. Filed FI3-26 for that change. The card is card-dc63473a-5.

The user's words, verbatim - these outrank every elaboration below, including your own:
one feature ask - when i enter a reply in a card, the card should get dismissed first, and reappear when it's updated

tasks.goal: Trace card reply and update lifecycle and propose how to hide a card on submitted reply and restore it when updated without losing the thread.
tasks.intent_json: {"goal":"Trace card reply and update lifecycle and propose how to hide a card on submitted reply and restore it when updated without losing the thread.","userWords":"one feature ask - when i enter a reply in a card, the card should get dismissed first, and reappear when it's updated","constraints":[{"kind":"read-only"}]}
tasks.outcome:
Hide the card in the shell when a reply is sent, and bring the same open card back when its content changes. Do not dismiss it. A real dismiss closes the thread's card, and a later update cannot restore that conversation as the same card.

What happens today

Entering a reply never leaves the stage. ReplyRow in src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx sends on Enter or the send control through useShellStore.sendReply (src/renderer/src/app/store.ts around line 682). That is the only reply entry. It calls window.firstmate.cards.reply, which is fm:cards:reply in src/preload/index.ts and src/core/dispatcher.ts, and that calls CrewSupervisor.replyToCard (src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts around line 3582).

replyToCard keeps the card open. It trims the text (an image-only reply is stored as "sent a picture"), refuses a blank reply, a reply over 4,000 characters, a host card (cardTakesReplies in src/shared/cards.ts), an unknown card, and a card already gone from the open set. It appends one captain row through addCardMessage, the single writer of card_messages, and pushes fm:cards:thread. A crewmate card is a captain steer with via "thread" and the card id, not awaited. A Firstmate card calls converseAboutCard, a captain turn about that card. chosen_action stays unset. The test "resolves nothing: the card and its buttons stay exactly where they were" in src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.test.ts pins that. tests/e2e/card-threads.spec.ts then expects the thread column to open beside the card and stay there until the author revises the title.

An update is a second emit_card with the same id, not a new card. upsertEmittedCard (same file, around line 3448) finds the open card, keeps createdAt, writes card_revisions when title, body, or actions change (CardStore.revise), and if the thread already has a message appends one host line, "revised: <title>". It then scheduleCardBroadcast (about 60ms). A prose answer is the other legal path: replyFromCrewmate or recordFirstmateThreadAnswer appends a crewmate or firstmate message and does not touch the card head. CARD_REPLY in src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts says a reply resolves nothing, and the author must not close the card because the captain replied.

The shell already knows how to take an open card off the stage and put it back when it changes. visibleCards hides any id in collapsedCardIds. reconcileStack (src/renderer/src/app/store.ts around line 164) keeps an id collapsed only while that card is still open and collapsedDigests[id] still equals cardDigest (title, body, action ids). A different digest drops the id, and if the stack was already seeded the card returns as unread, like an arrival, without stealing the card on screen. store.test.ts "brings a collapsed note back unread when it is revised in place, and only then" pins that a status-only push does not bring it back. Threads are a separate map, threads[cardId], filled by the reply result and by onThread. Collapsing a card does not clear that map or card_messages. When the card is shown again, CardLayer in src/renderer/src/app/HomeScreen.tsx opens the thread column if messages.length > 0. applyThread already reopens a closed thread column when a message arrives, because an answer the captain cannot see is worse than a column.

Why a real dismiss cannot do this

CrewSupervisor.close (around line 6310) is the captain's ×. It deletes the card from the open set, resolves the row as "close", and recordCardResolution records "dismissed". That writes a feed line, "captain dismissed the card", lists the card under captain resolutions, closes an answer task done/answered (closeAnsweredTask), and drops a Firstmate decision task as cancelled. replyToCard then throws "Card is closed; its thread takes no more replies." A later emit_card with the same id does not revise in place. The open-card branch is skipped, so there is no "revised:" line and no card_revisions row. cardStore.reopen only clears resolved_at, then the card is minted again with a new createdAt. card_messages survive a resolve (they die only in deleteForTask), but the open-card facts do not: threadAwaitingCrewmate and hasDecisionCard read only this.cards. Hiding by resolving would also make the whose-turn rule forget that the captain is waiting on an answer.

Proposal

On submit, hide in sendReply before the round trip returns. After the empty and in-flight guards, put the card id in collapsedCardIds and set collapsedDigests[id] to cardDigest of the card as it stands. The digest is required: reconcileStack drops an id whose stored digest is missing, so the next cards snapshot would show the card again even though nothing changed. Recompute phase with derivePhase so an empty stage is not left "working". Leave threads, card_messages, buttons, and the core open set alone. Do not call cards.close.

Clear the draft only after fm:cards:reply resolves, as today. On refusal, remove the id from collapsedCardIds and show replyErrors with the draft still there. A refused reply must not look dismissed.

Restore on update is the digest check that already exists. Do not add a second restore flag. The cards snapshot after upsertEmittedCard changes title, body, or action ids, reconcileStack drops the collapsed id, and the same card returns with the same id, the same createdAt, and the thread still in memory. If it is the only card, it is the one on screen. If another card is up, it returns unread and the notice pulse fires, which is the existing arrival rule. A push that does not change the digest, including status streaming, keeps it hidden.

A prose answer does not change the digest, so the card would stay off stage and the answer would be invisible. When applyThread receives a message whose who is crewmate or firstmate for a collapsed id, drop that id from collapsedCardIds and from collapsedDigests. Do not do that for a host line. The "revised:" push is sent before the debounced cards snapshot, and unhiding on it would flash the old body for up to 60ms. The digest change brings the revised card back already updated. A captain row must not unhide either.

The thread is not lost because nothing in this path resolves the card, deletes card_messages, or clears threads[cardId]. loadThread still short-circuits when that map entry exists, and after a relaunch it reads cardThread from the core. collapsedCardIds is memory only, same as note collapse, so a relaunch shows the card again with its thread. Do not add a column for that.

Out of scope for the hide: the Now row can still name the open card, and focusCard already removes a collapsed id, so clicking that row brings it back before an update. That is the existing escape, not a second mechanism. Author close_card and the captain's × after focusing still resolve for real. A second reply is possible only after the card is back.

Tests the next step should change

src/renderer/src/app/store.test.ts: sending a reply collapses a decision, not only a note; a same-digest snapshot keeps it collapsed; a body or title or action change brings that same id back unread without dropping threads[cardId]; a refusal unhides and keeps the draft; a crewmate or firstmate thread message unhides; a host "revised:" message does not.

tests/e2e/card-threads.spec.ts currently expects the thread column to appear as soon as the reply is sent and to stay up through the revision. After this, the card and the thread column leave on send and both return together when the title updates, with the captain line and the "revised:" line still in the thread, and the decision button still enabled. The core test that replyToCard resolves nothing should stay as it is. The hide is not a resolution.
tasks.outcome_summary: Hide the card in the shell when a reply is sent, and bring the same open card back when its content changes.

tasks.intent_json: {"goal":"Inspect card thread rendering and crewmate lifecycle signals, then propose a clear working spinner for active thread handling.","userWords":"also, in this card thread view, if the crewmate is working we should render some form of a spinner showing it's being worked on","constraints":[{"kind":"read-only"}]}
tasks.outcome:
Show a working crewmate glyph at the foot of a card thread while that card's crewmate is working. Do not add a chrome spinner, a thread-message row, or a local "reply in flight" flag.

Intent. In the card thread view, if the crewmate is working, show that the thread is being worked on. Working means the same thing the orbit already uses: that task's activity is `starting` or `running`.

What is missing. `src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx` paints a head (`THREAD` plus `card.meta`), `MessageList`, and `ReplyRow`. Nothing there reads task activity, `firstmateBusy`, or the orbit. `HomeScreen.tsx` `CardLayer` passes `cardId`, `author={card.meta}`, and width into `CardThread`. The in-place rung (`StackedCard`, stage under 720px, unreachable at the 960px window minimum) swaps the body for the same `MessageList`. A thread opens only after the first message (`threadOpen` in `CardLayer`). Host cards have no reply row (`cardTakesReplies`).

The signal, already on the wire. A crewmate is a `work` task. `crewStatusOf` in `src/renderer/src/character/crew/crewSignal.ts` is working when `TaskView.activity` is `starting` or `running`, idle otherwise (`idle`, `interrupted`, null). That is the split the orbit paints and the one `task_changed` already carries (`src/shared/events.ts`: `activity` plus `kind`, `status`, `taskId`). `setActivity` (`src/core/tasks/taskService.ts`) patches the row, and `TaskProtocol.onChange` broadcasts `task_changed` after the commit. Lifecycle: `claimForDispatch` / `dispatch` set `starting`; `CrewSupervisor.beginTurn` sets `running` and runtime state `streaming`; `turnComplete` sets `idle` and runtime `idle` together (`crewSupervisor.ts` around 2284 and 2364). `crewCounts()` is the strip's aggregate (runtime not idle, plus resumable leftovers as idle) and has no task id, so it cannot drive one thread. `crewOrbit().statusOf(id)` is the same fact but a module ref with no React subscription, and a crewmate that has left the ring is absent, so do not read it from render.

Why the thread does not update today. `store.ts` `init` subscribes to `events.on` → `applyEvent`, which forwards `task_changed` only into `applyCrewEvent` (orbit side channel) and stores `firstmateBusy` from `firstmate_state`. The boot `tasks.board()` fetch seeds the orbit and is not kept. The `fm:tasks` push is consumed by the panel read executor, not the shell store. A thread push (`fm:cards:thread`) only replaces `threads[cardId]`.

When a reply becomes working. `replyToCard` (`crewSupervisor.ts`) writes the captain message and pushes the thread immediately, then steers without awaiting. A crewmate card calls `steerCrewmate` with `via: "thread"` and `cardId`. A live idle session is delivered and `beginTurn` flips activity to `running` before the model answers, so the glyph covers the whole turn. An already streaming session is already `running` (a mid-turn steer does not add a second indicator; a Cursor followup-queue steer waits in that same turn). A session that must resume stays idle until `resumeTask` reaches `beginTurn`. A failed delivery is a feed line (`Could not deliver the reply on "…"`) and never becomes working. The turn ending sets `idle` whether the answer was `reply()`, a card revision (host "revised:" line), or silence. `sendingReplies` only covers the reply IPC, which returns before the steer, so it must not drive the glyph.

Do not conflate working with "owes an answer". Whose-turn branch 0 (`src/core/orchestrator/reportSort.ts`, `docs/report-sort.md`) is an unanswered captain message. That is not activity. An idle crewmate with the captain's last message and no glyph is the honest picture. An interrupted crewmate is not working.

What to draw. The design skill forbids spinning UI chrome (`readme.md` Motion; `Button.prompt.md`: pending is static "Working...", no spinner). The only perpetual motion is the Firstmate and crewmate structures. The spinner is the existing working crewmate: the crew strip's 22px glyph (`src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/crew/crew.frame.js`, `GLYPH_SIZE = 22`, `aria-label` `Crewmate - working`), ember `--wire-hot`, fast double spin, one still frame under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keep it ≤32px. Do not add a Lucide loader, a CSS `@keyframes` spin, or a third copy of the tetrahedron if `drawCrewmate` / the strip glyph can be reused. Do not write a `card_messages` row. Place one host row at the foot of `MessageList` (so the beside column and the in-place list share it), same two-column grid, who `crew` in `--accent`, word `working` in mono `--fg-3`, no timestamp. `data-thread-working` and `aria-busy` for the test. It leaves when activity leaves. Buttons stay pinned; a reply still resolves nothing (`CardThread.prompt.md`).

Wiring. Seed a `crewActivity` map in the shell store from the boot `tasks.board()` already fetched in `init` (work rows only), and update it from `task_changed` when `kind === "work"` (`activity`, drop the key when `status !== "active"`). Pass `working` into `CardThread` and the in-place `MessageList` from `CardLayer`: `card.author === "crewmate"` and `crewStatusOf(crewActivity[card.taskId]) === "working"`. Pass `taskId`, not only `card.meta`. Same row for a Firstmate card from the store's existing `firstmateBusy` (`firstmate_state`, set in `firstmateAgent.ts` when `converse` actually prompts, including `converseAboutCard`). No new IPC, no new activity enum, no thread schema change. One sentence in `CardThread.prompt.md` so the skill owns the rule.

Not this. Do not show it on the reply row before a thread exists, on a closed thread column, on host cards, or for `idle` / `interrupted` / null. Do not light it the instant Send is clicked. Do not key it on the newest message still being the captain's.

Verified by reading, not by running the app. Files: `src/renderer/src/cards/CardThread.tsx`, `src/renderer/src/app/HomeScreen.tsx` (`CardLayer`, `StackedCard`), `src/renderer/src/app/store.ts` (`threads`, `applyEvent`, boot `board()`), `src/renderer/src/character/crew/crewSignal.ts` (`crewStatusOf`), `src/shared/events.ts` (`task_changed.activity`), `src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts` (`beginTurn`, `turnComplete`, `replyToCard`, `crewCounts`), `src/core/tasks/taskService.ts` (`setActivity`, `claimForDispatch`), `docs/card-threads.md`, `.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/cards/CardThread.prompt.md`, `components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md`, `components/core/Button.prompt.md`. Existing thread e2e `tests/e2e/card-threads.spec.ts` asserts `[data-card-thread]` and messages only; it does not cover activity. A reproduction is: open a crewmate card that already has a message, send a reply, and watch the column — the captain line arrives on `fm:cards:thread` and the orbit heats on the later `task_changed`, and the column never changes between those two.

Risk of the proposal: low. It reuses the activity the orbit already paints and adds one host row. The only lie to avoid is a local pending flag across resume or a failed steer.

tasks.outcome:
The Tasks panel section expand control is the caret on a collapsed group header, not the panel’s own Expand Tasks button. It is the span.caret inside the button [data-now-group-header] in src/renderer/src/plugins/builtin/now/now.frame.js (line 270: caret.textContent = "›", U+203A SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK, aria-hidden="true"). Only charted and landed are collapsible; waiting and underway are open by default and have no caret. Collapsed, the mark points right. Open, now.html line 66 rotates it 90deg so it points down: [data-now-group-header][aria-expanded="true"] .caret { transform: rotate(90deg); }. The button already carries aria-expanded and its accessible name is the group label plus the count. The same right mark and quarter-turn are copied in .claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/now/NowPanel.jsx line 37. SidePanelChrome’s Expand Tasks control is a different button: a down chevron (path "m6 9 6 6 6-6") rotated 180deg while collapsed, so it already points up. Disclosure.tsx’s path "m9 18 6-6-6-6" is also a right chevron, but Settings uses it, not Tasks. No test asserts the glyph; tests/e2e/now-panel.spec.ts only checks aria-expanded and whether the rows appear.

Smallest accessible change: in now.frame.js set caret.textContent from the same open bit that sets aria-expanded — "↑" (U+2191) when closed, "↓" (U+2193) when open — and keep aria-hidden="true". Do not add an aria-label; that would replace the label-and-count name, and a visible arrow would be announced as "upwards arrow" if it were not hidden. In now.html delete the rotate(90deg) rule. Leaving it turns the new up arrow into a right arrow when the group is open, which is the thing being rejected. A CSS-only rotate(-90deg) on "›" is smaller but still ships a right-pointing character and falls back to right if transforms are ignored. Mirror the same two states in NowPanel.jsx so the design skill does not keep the right mark. Do not change SidePanelChrome or Disclosure.tsx.

tasks.outcome:
When a project's Care is Default, a task that actually ships a change is done carefully (standard), unless the captain's own words name another care, and a second look is cut back to carefully when the change does not leave as a proposed change. Default is not a fourth care level. Settings stores it as no standing rigor (repos.rigor null; the pill value is derive). Talking configure_repo rigor default does the same. The host then derives care at the moment the work starts, in src/shared/rigor.ts rigorFor, called from CrewSupervisor.deriveRigor. The first rule that applies wins. The project's standing rigor is skipped because Default left it empty.

Nothing at all, before any ask. Care exists only for crewmate work that lands a change through a gate. No care is stamped, and the brief says Rigor: none, when the task is not work, when its kind is review, when the project is the personal workspace (builds in place; Care shows none, not Default), or when the deliverable is an answer. An answer is a plan, research, or reproduce kind, or a read-only constraint. An ask for a second look does not create a care level on those.

The captain's words, if any. Firstmate passes rigor_ask only when the person said how careful to be: quick, standard, or reviewed. There is no phrase table in the host. Omit it and this rule does not fire. That ask beats everything below it.

The posture bound, under the ask. Reviewed means a second look of the branch before a proposed change. If the task is not shipping as a proposed change (the project's posture, or a delivery_ask of local-only for this task alone), an asked-for second look becomes carefully, and the reason says why. Quickly on a straight-in project stays quickly. Posture never picks care on its own.

Otherwise carefully. Reason: every repository ships standard by default. Same tier as an explicit Care of carefully, different reason (the repository ships standard). Direct-pr and local-only both land here. A task with no project does too: no repository reads as local-only, still carefully.

What does not move it. The model tier, a named model, premium, difficulty, and an escalation do not add ceremony. Escalation also does not copy the previous task's rigor or rigor_ask; a fresh attempt with no new words is derived again, so on Default it is carefully unless the new spawn repeats the ask. A care already stamped on the task is kept on a later start; changing Care after that does not rewrite it. A queued task takes the derivation of the moment it starts.

Examples, Care left on Default. Fix the meter, no words, proposed changes: carefully. Same, no project: carefully. Just do it quickly: quickly. Review this before it lands, proposed changes: with a second look. Same words, or delivery_ask local-only: carefully, because there is no proposed change to look at. What does this do, read-only: no care. A review task: no care. Personal workspace: no care.

Caveat: spawn_crewmate's rigor_ask description still says the host derives care from the posture and the intelligence tier. That sentence is stale. rigorFor does not read the intelligence tier, and posture only cuts a second look back to carefully. The derivation tests are src/shared/rigor.test.ts and the order case in crewSupervisor.test.ts.

tasks.outcome:
Root cause: the failed live-main lookup was a crewmate’s direct `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`, not a host-managed GitHub operation. FI3-35’s recorded outcome says it failed for lack of GitHub sign-in; its final card used cached `origin/main` at `e2b0893` and said live main was unverified, without a sign-in action. I did not retry the network lookup or inspect credentials, so the exact underlying git stderr and whether the failure was missing credentials rather than another access problem are not independently established.

The sign-in gate only handles model-provider authentication. `src/core/orchestrator/crewSupervisor.ts:3867-3876` raises an auth card on a failed *model session* when `isAuthFailureMessage(error)` matches; `src/core/orchestrator/firstmateAgent.ts:2322-2333` does likewise for Firstmate’s model session. `src/shared/authFailure.ts:1-19` explicitly excludes tool and bash output. `crewSupervisor.ts:3994-4027` sends these cards to Subscriptions or restores a provider account, not GitHub. Crewmate git commands therefore cannot trigger that gate, and the crewmate’s report of failure is not an auth signal to it. The only agent-declared open effects are Settings and Subscriptions (`src/shared/cards.ts:36-40`, `src/core/pi/cardTool.ts:64-70,165-170`, `src/core/claude/claudeCardTool.ts:62-68`); `src/renderer/src/app/store.ts:623-630` only routes those sections. Projects has no GitHub sign-in control (`src/renderer/src/settings/ProjectsTab.tsx`). `src/core/workspace/workspaceService.ts:285-339` independently fetches with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and falls back to stale refs on failure; that dispatch-time fetch is not the crewmate’s read-only live-head lookup. `src/core/orchestrator/prCi.ts:172-240` uses gh for PR checks but converts errors into text, without a GitHub auth handoff.

Failing check reproduced on this checkout without accessing GitHub: temporarily create `src/shared/githubSignIn.repro.test.ts` containing `import { it, expect } from 'vitest'; import { agentEffectSchema } from './cards'; it('offers GitHub sign-in', () => { expect(agentEffectSchema.safeParse({kind:'open',target:'projects',signIn:'github'}).success).toBe(true); });`, then run `pnpm exec vitest run src/shared/githubSignIn.repro.test.ts`. Result: 1 failed, expected true, received false. This exercises the actual card-action contract at the missing handoff, rather than the live credential state. I removed the scratch test; `git status --short` is empty. Next step FI3-39 should add an explicit GitHub auth-required path for git/gh failures, a captain-facing sign-in action backed by an actual GitHub sign-in flow, and an end-to-end test with a fake unauthenticated GitHub operation proving that the sign-in offer appears and the task can resume afterward; keep model-provider sign-in separate.

tasks.outcome:
The running app asks its decision model one question, in one place: what kind of work this is, once, just before a crewmate starts. The old triage session does not call it. The fallback is not a third model. It is the same cheap signed-in model that answers by default. This is from the current code, not a live run, so which concrete model a given install binds first depends on what is signed in.

Two doors reach the call: an immediate start (commission), and a queued start when its wait ends (dispatchQueuedTask via classifyQueued), including a crewmate’s follow-up. Asked at most once. Skipped, with no model call, when a model was named, a premium ask was made, the work is a stronger-model retry, or it is a review. A report is sorted by a rule. No decide call exists on that path. Settings only stores the pick. An offline scoring script can ask the same question and is not the running app. No second question was found.

The call returns one word: plan, research, reproduce, implement, fix, chore, or unclear. It does not pick the crewmate. The table then maps the word: plan, research, and reproduce high; implement and fix high unless a verified basis makes them medium; chore low; unclear high.

By default the answerer is the cheapest signed-in model, low group then medium then high, premium only if named, the Firstmate’s own account last. Effort is fixed at low, the same request FI3-59 set, now on the question session. The Pi one-shot passes low through and does not step it down, unlike a crewmate. A model with no usable effort level is marked non-reasoning first, so no effort parameter is sent. Whether some other provider rejects a bare low request was not traced past that. On Claude the app still asks for low, but thinking stays off because the answer is capped at 64, under the 1024 thinking floor. One turn, one retry, 15 second bound.

Jev is optional and off until turned on (row names it, egress on, consent covers the fact set, a key is stored). The request names jev-latest and has no effort setting. Below 0.6 certainty it declines. If it cannot answer, the cheap model answers and the record says so. A rejected key writes one note, once. Later calls still try Jev, fail, and fall back.

If nothing can answer, the kind is unclear, a high crewmate still starts, and there is no card. The wait stops at 15 seconds. The card is the drawn version.

tasks.outcome:
reproduced: yes. The failing check is that a bent connector's interior stays unpainted. On a clean page using the card styling and the stored line data, the branch interior was rgba(152, 164, 189, 255) and the bend interior was the same grey, stroke rgb(255, 162, 87). Both hits were the line. The check exited 1. Told not to fill, those points were the page ground. With only that fill declaration removed, both interiors were black, rgba(0, 0, 0, 255).

The cause is both, and it is not a rewrite of the drawing. Authors draw an open bend with a stroke and no fill. A drawing fills an open path by closing it, so the bend becomes a triangle. The card styling sets fill to the secondary text color on every drawing (`svg { color: var(--fg-2); fill: currentColor }` in `src/renderer/src/plugins/frames/frameStylesheet.ts`), which is why the triangle is grey rather than black. Both card frames insert the markup unchanged and use that styling. The branch still stored on card-77fa7f1c-fm-midturn-message-answer is `M180 51h174M261 51v50h93`. The bend as first drawn is `M342 72 V105 H383` with a warn stroke and no fill. The current checkout card adds `fill="none"`. The same bend is still stored as `M385 69 V103 H507`. Of 70 stored cards, 64 have a drawing and 27 already turn fill off on a bent line.

The fix belongs in the card styling, with the writing note corrected in the same change. Guidance never says to turn fill off, and the design note that puts `fill="currentColor"` on the drawing root paints this grey by itself. Guidance alone does not stop a forgotten line. A measured change that blanks only path, polyline, and line elements that set no fill of their own stops the triangle and leaves explicit fills and label colors alone. Blanking every line wipes arrowheads. Setting the whole drawing to no fill hides labels that set no fill. FI3-98 is the existing task for the fix. The answer card asks whether to fix the styling and the note, or only the writing guidance.

Built this worktree, then launched a throwaway app (mock subscription, fake microphone, voice model marked ready, no shared data) and ran `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/repro-voice-press.spec.ts --project=desktop --reporter=line`. The check held right Option until the waveform and Abandon control were on screen, then released and saw the idle hint return (`type, or press/hold right ⌥ to talk`). It then tapped right Option for 80ms and waited 200ms. Talking was off: Abandon count 0, character idle, hint back. A second 80ms tap did the same. The failing check, at tests/e2e/repro-voice-press.spec.ts:91, was `expect(afterQuick.abandon, "quick press should leave talking started").toBe(1)` — expected 1, received 0. The run exited 1. Screenshots: during the hold the pill is a live waveform with abandon, accept, and submit; after release and after the quick press the pill is the idle hint again. The note titled Microphone access on those later shots is the first-use primer from the hold, not a talking session.

A listener registered after the app's own key listeners recorded the same three gestures (hold, first tap, second tap). Each down left the screen Listening with Abandon present. Each up cleared Abandon. So a quick press does start talking for the key-down, then the key-up ends it. The second press starts and ends another short hold. It never meets a session that is still running.

Where that happens. src/renderer/src/app/App.tsx lines 49-58, unchanged since the shell landed (f7c8f722). On keydown, if the key is Alt at location 2 and not a repeat, it calls startRecording. On keyup, if the key is Alt at location 2 and the phase is recording, it calls acceptRecording. No timer, no threshold, no mode flag. startRecording in src/renderer/src/app/store.ts returns immediately if a recording is already on, so a second press cannot mean "stop" except by the keyup that follows, and that keyup only fires after a press that already ended the previous session. The design mock (`.claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/ui_kits/firstmate/AppShell.jsx`) starts on keydown and never stops on keyup; the app does not follow that.

Not the mode switch, established by reading only. src/renderer/src/voice/voiceController.ts drops a finished clip shorter than 0.4 seconds (MIN_CLIP_SECONDS) and returns no transcript. That runs after the session has already ended. This run did not transcribe, so it does not show that drop. It is not what chooses press versus hold.

The green field is gone. It was a borderless test window I had put over the main display, plus a scratch copy of the app; both are closed, the desktop picture was not changed, and the installed app is back at its previous frame. Nothing of mine is on screen.

reproduced: yes. On current main 07d3c660 (release 0.1.16, which contains change #400), a shown launch does not open a view through to the desktop at any wash, including 0. The page wash itself is not the opaque layer.

Established, from a clean shown launch of the built app (scratch home and scratch user data, macOS 26.6.2, not the windowless test harness). The page is marked translucent, and Reduce transparency is off. Setting the wash through the app's appearance setting changes only the page:

- dark 0: body color is fully transparent; page pixels at the corners have alpha 0
- dark 35: body alpha 0.273; page pixels about rgba(3, 6, 11, 0.275)
- dark 100: body alpha 0.780; page pixels about rgba(4, 5, 15, 0.780)
- light 0: body fully transparent; page corner alpha 0
- light 35: body alpha 0.273; page pixels about rgba(241, 243, 246, 0.275)
- light 100: body alpha 0.780; page pixels about rgba(241, 244, 249, 0.780)

The failing check is the composited window, not that page paint. From inside the running app, at dark wash 0, an 8×8 screen sample inside the window bounds was opaque rgb(46, 47, 46), alpha 255 — flat gray, not the desktop. The same process's picture of its own window is 960×1380, and the top-left pixels of that picture are alpha 0, so the page really is clear there; what remains on screen is the window behind it.

What is behind the page, read from the running window:

- The window background color is the system window background, rgb(30, 30, 30), alpha 1. The window is not marked opaque, but that color is fully opaque. The app asked for background #00000000 and did not set a transparent window.
- The content view is marked opaque. Its own layer color is clear.
- Clear system glass is present (style clear, corner radius 8) as the back subview. Its content view is empty. The web view sits in front of it.
- Change #400 is what removed the older under-window material on macOS 26 and added this glass view. The glass is behind the page; it is not what covers the desktop. The opaque window background is.

Candidate, not a separate measurement: the background alpha is ignored because the window was never made transparent, which is when that alpha is honored, and the older see-through material is no longer requested on this macOS. The glass view's public role is to embed a content view, and the running one has none, so it is not acting as a window backdrop. I did not prove the glass plate itself is opaque; the measured opaque layer is the window background.

Outside screen captures cannot see app windows from this session, so they only showed the desktop wallpaper and do not count. A known-color field behind the window would settle the last visual doubt, but that is what covered the screen, so I stopped. I would need permission to put one small window over a corner of the desktop, not a full-screen field. The installed app's wash was not changed.

tasks.outcome:
The captain's guess holds: figure type looks big because the 11 px refusal from FI3-107 (#394) measures type at the narrowest 350 px figure column, while a card on the stage alone is 560 px wide and gives a 510 px column. Type sized to be 11 px at 350 px draws at 16 px at 510 px, above the 14 px body text, so no figure can pass the check and still match the body; and the refusal's advice to use a smaller viewBox sent authors to 350-unit drawings, where every unit is 1.46 px. Measured over the stored cards on this Mac (85 with a drawing, 61 with measurable text): before #394, 53 cards, mostly 480 to 720 units wide, median label 11.1 px in the usual column; after #394, 8 cards, seven of them 350 or 360 units wide, median label 18.4 px, range 16.0 to 21.3 px. The reported card (0.1.18 tagged) measures 17 to 19.8 px in a 560 px card and 11.7 to 13.6 px in a 400 px card, the width its author was made to size for. Renders were made in Playwright's headless Chromium with the frame's own stylesheet and fonts, never in the app window; the browser's measured sizes matched the arithmetic within 0.1 px and the reported card matches the screenshot. Pictures and the lab script live under lab/figtype in the working copy (ignored) and in a temp copy of the database; nothing was committed, pushed or opened.

The plan, as one card with three directions and direction 2 as the default. Shared authoring rule for all three: a full-width drawing is 510 units wide so one unit is one pixel in the usual card; labels use the app's own sizes, unsized for 12.5 px, 14 px for the one that matters, 11 px mono for micro labels. Direction 1, draw at true size: guidance and the check only, no frame change; a smaller drawing gets its pixel width instead of 100 percent so the frame only shrinks; the check asks for declared type of at least 11 px and a drawing no wider than 510 units; labels shrink with the drawing in a narrow card (about 8.6 px at 400 px); reaches new cards only. Direction 2 (default), type follows the drawing down to 11 px and never past its declared size: the same rule plus a small change in the frame's bridge script, which already observes its size; it measures each drawing's scale and keeps every label between 11 px and its declared size while shapes keep scaling; the check drops the column arithmetic and keeps the two shape rules; reaches stored cards too (the reported card draws at 12 to 14 px, the pre-#394 tiny ones lift to 11 px). Direction 3, type holds its size: the same frame change but labels never shrink; simplest to state, reaches stored cards, crowds boxes sooner in narrow cards.

Questions asked on the card, each with my answer: (1) should the fix reach stored cards, yes, 53 of 61 draw under 11 px and 8 over 16 px, only a frame change reaches them; (2) should labels shrink in a narrow card, a little, never under 11 px; (3) does the card-time check stay, yes, simplified to declared type at least 11 px and a full-width drawing at most 510 units, no column arithmetic; (4) which sizes should the guidance name, the app's own, 12.5 unsized, 14 for the one that matters, 11 mono micro, never larger than body text unless a deliberate display number; (5) should the 328 px card (both rails docked at the 960 px minimum window, a 278 px column the check does not know about) count, direction 2 gives it 11 px labels, direction 1 gives 6.8 px, which I would accept as a rare layout. Waiting on question 3: whether a drawing wider than 510 units is refused outright or only shrunk with its type floored.

Assumptions: the usual card is 560 px (design width) giving 510 px; the 400 px card happens only with a thread beside it when the free stage is 720 to 952 px; well-proportioned means 12.5 to 14 px labels beside 14 px body text; the 61 stored figures stand for what authors do; directions 2 and 3 were simulated in the lab, the frame change itself was not built.

Spec for the next step under the default (direction 2), so it can be checked: in src/shared/plugins/bridge.ts beside the existing ResizeObserver, for every drawing with a viewBox, after layout and on each resize, keep each text element's drawn size (SVG text and tspan, and flowing text in foreignObject) at min(declared, max(11 px, declared times scale)), and re-pin FRAME_BRIDGE_SHA256 with its test; in src/core/pi/cardLint.ts replace the 350 px arithmetic (MIN_FIGURE_WIDTH) with two shape rules, declared type at least 11 px and a full-width drawing at most 510 units, each refusal naming the fix; in cardContract.ts line 60, Viz.prompt.md (Scaling, Type) and docs/card-authoring.md lines 431 to 438 replace the multiply-by-column paragraph with the one authoring rule; run pnpm replay:gate since the prompt and the check change. Done looks like: the reported stored card draws labels at 12 to 14 px in a 560 px card and 11 px in a 400 px card; the stored 630-unit card draws at 11 px; a new 720-unit figure with 11 px type is refused for its width, not its type; a test renders a drawing in the frame at both widths and asserts those sizes. Leaves alone: the card geometry and thread ladder, the picture rules, FI3-106. Out of scope: guessing whether a label spills its box, figures a card's own script draws later, the light theme. Under direction 1 the frame and bridge are untouched and the check's floor moves to the usual column; under direction 3 the bridge holds every label at its declared size.

tasks.outcome: The window uses macOS blur behind a theme-colored wash: shown macOS 26+ windows install clear NSGlassEffectView, earlier versions use Electron under-window vibrancy, and other/hidden windows stay opaque. Window wash is 0–100% of a 78%-opaque dark/light tint; a higher tint alpha makes it more opaque but not blurrier, while Reduce transparency makes it solid. The new focus-state finding is version-specific: on older macOS the app currently forces vibrancy state active, but Electron offers inactive as a creation option, and Apple's NSVisualEffectView documents that state as always showing the inactive look, including when focused. On macOS 26+ the installed NSGlassEffectView has no public state property—only regular/clear style and tint color—so setting vibrancy's inactive option would not affect the current glass path. Neither API offers a fractional active/inactive blend or a blur-radius dial. A tunable color/opacity overlay could approximate an in-between background without fading the UI, but cannot guarantee the inactive blur; alternative materials, style, or replacing glass with a native visual-effect view need shown-window comparisons, and the cause of the captain's observed inactive appearance has not been measured. Verified from app code, Electron's installed type definitions and macOS 26.5 SDK headers; no tests or visual comparisons were run and nothing changed.
tasks.outcome_summary: The inactive look can be forced for older macOS vibrancy, but macOS 26 clear glass has no documented inactive override or blend; an adjustable tint can only approximate it.

verdict: findings

F1, warning, src/renderer/src/app/HomeScreen.tsx:964-969: the whole prompt dock gets `filter: var(--acrylic-blur)` whenever any record is open. That includes the input, the draft, the feed whisper and the recording pill during a right-⌥ capture. It happens even when the pane doesn't cover the composer. In the default 1200×800 window the composer sits at about y 652–704. A short record opened from a top now-panel row ends around y 420, so the composer blurs with nothing over it. The spec has to shrink the window to its minimum to get any overlap at all. The builder's Risk line ("softens for the full time a task record is open") doesn't make this clear, and the 350×320 before/after crops only show the overlapping case. Action: ask-user. The options are to blur only while the revealed pane actually covers the dock, or to accept the current behavior after the captain sees a default-size shot.

F2, warning, docs/translucent-window.md:31-35 and HomeScreen.tsx:964: the stated cause is unverified. The comment and doc say the pane's backdrop samples only the native material, not the composited page. If that's true, the fix is incomplete, because the same pane also sits over the centre card, which "stays up beside it". At 1200×800 the card spans about x 170–730 and the pane about x 368–888. It also sits over the notices hung under the composer (ComposerNotice, VoiceNotice, DiagnosticsNotice, HomeScreen.tsx:1027-1029). None of these are blurred, and no evidence checks them against the captain's words ("doesn't have any background blur like the main cards"). If the cause is something about the composer specifically, then the comment and doc are wrong. Action: ask-user. Capture a shown-window shot with a card behind the pane. Then either extend the fix or correct the explanation.

F3, warning, .claude/skills/firstmate-3000-design/components/voice/VoiceInput.prompt.md:9: the design system's composer rule still says "The shell stays clear at every height - its hairline alone, never acrylic, never blur", and the change contradicts it. Only readme.md was amended. NowDetailPane.prompt.md:12 ("it does not dim or blur the character") also doesn't mention that the pane now blurs the composer. Action: auto-fix. If the blur stays, amend both lines to match the readme.

F4, info, HomeScreen.tsx:897/967: the blur keys on `record !== null`, so it lands before NowDetailPane reveals itself. The pane stays at opacity 0 until the frame body reports its height and placement settles. So the composer blurs a beat before the pane appears. If the body never reports, the composer stays blurred with no visible pane until the next click. Action: ask-user (small visible ordering glitch).

F5, info, HomeScreen.tsx:966-969: reading `document.documentElement.dataset.windowMaterial` during render repeats the attribute name `WINDOW_MATERIAL_ATTRIBUTE` owns (src/shared/windowMaterial.ts). It also splits material styling between JS and styles.css. A `data-record-open` hook on the dock plus an `html[data-window-material="translucent"]` rule in design/styles.css would do the same thing in one place. Action: auto-fix.

Checklist: readme.md (F3 covers its sibling docs), both artifact PNGs (overlap-only crops, F1/F2), docs/translucent-window.md (F2), HomeScreen.tsx (F1, F2, F4, F5), tests/e2e/record-controls.spec.ts. The spec is sound for what it claims: overlap at the minimum size, a blur filter while the record is open and emulated translucent, and the blur cleared on close. It can't show the visual result, because end-to-end test windows are opaque. It doesn't cover the case where the pane doesn't overlap the composer. Where the builder's record looks wrong: the Risk line understates the case where nothing covers the composer, and the stated cause isn't established by the evidence.

tasks.outcome:
Intent
Proposed spec, awaiting agreement: let the captain close charted work he no longer wants without starting it, claiming completion, or deleting its record. FI3-208 is the verified example: open work, on request, ready, found on FI3-207, with no reported children or blocking links.

What changed
No project files changed. One illustrated decision card records two directions and three independent numbered questions, with these proposed answers: (1) A, confirm every close inline rather than B, one-click close for simple tasks; (2) wording Close task rather than Drop task; (3) confirmed cascade of unstarted parts rather than refusing until each part is handled separately. Changed picks go through Revise these choices so the full spec can be updated before agreement.

The complete proposed build spec is:
1. Scope: all open, never-started work records, including on-request, blocked, automatically queued and parent/container tasks. Guard never-started state at the host, not just the rendered button. Other record kinds, closed tasks, and previously started work remain unchanged.
2. Placement: use the existing host footer, right-aligned; secondary Close task immediately before primary Start wherever Start already applies. Preserve current Start eligibility and disabled blocker behavior. Parents or other eligible records without Start have Close task alone. The top-right cross remains popover dismissal and never closes the task; its accessible wording should distinguish that gesture from Close task. Do not change popover geometry, acrylic, anchoring or body hierarchy.
3. Recommended confirmation: Close task replaces the footer with 'Close FI3-208? It won’t start. Its record stays.' and Cancel / Close task. The confirming close uses the existing danger-outline style; Cancel gets focus and Enter must not implicitly approve. Cancel restores the initial footer and writes nothing. Dismissing the popover also writes nothing. No separate modal or required reason field. Names and counts of affected descendants and external waiting tasks must be visible in the confirmation, including that closing will not start unstarted dependent tasks.
4. Children: list all open descendants, including nested parts, before an explicit confirmed cascade. Drop those descendants deepest first as dropped/superseded, then the parent as dropped/cancelled, atomically. Closed descendants are untouched. Any live descendant that has started prevents the entire operation, with a plain explanation; no partial cascade and no active-work stop/discard from this control. Descendant reasons identify the parent. Under the alternate parts choice, refuse whenever open parts remain and leave every record unchanged.
5. Dependencies: do not remove blocks links, complete or drop external dependent tasks, or change informational/provenance links. External open dependents remain unready after a prerequisite is dropped; preserve the existing dead-blocker review, which can explicitly remove the edge, drop the dependent, or leave it planned. Active dependents are not stopped; preserve the existing exception that a dropped blocker no longer holds their close. Preserve ordinary ancestor-container completion and existing ready-sweep rules.
6. Execution: extend the existing typed task lifecycle boundary and guarded planned-drop path, with TaskService remaining the sole writer. Preserve captain attribution rather than calling the existing Firstmate-attributed drop path unchanged. Recheck task state and exactly the reviewed graph effects before writing; changed effects require a refreshed review, and a concurrent start must refuse. Disable competing controls immediately while pending. Duplicate submission cannot close twice. A refusal clears pending, explains the problem, and writes nothing. Retire only closed tasks' outstanding cards as obsolete, not as answered decisions.
7. Afterwards: keep the popover open on the retained record; show dropped, 'Dropped <relative time>: No longer wanted.', and Activity identifying that the captain closed it before it started. Preserve exact time on hover, the key, asks, goal, filing, links and timeline. Remove lifecycle controls. Remove the task from charted, never add it to done, and retain detail readability. No deletion, new history browser, Undo or reopen control.
8. Alternative B, if chosen: only a simple task with no open descendants and no live external dependents closes immediately; any graph effects still require explicit consequence confirmation. Keep all other safeguards and record outcomes above. Alternative wording Drop task changes action/confirmation wording, not stored semantics.

Explicit assumptions: scope includes all never-started work, not only the pictured on-request leaf; No longer wanted is a preset reason, not fabricated personal explanation; no Undo/reopen/reason-entry feature is added; incoming blockers do not forbid abandonment; existing active controls, task retention, graph rules and container completion remain unchanged. These assumptions are shown on the card and are part of the proposed agreement.

Verified
Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, the design skill, task graph/record/retention documentation, recordFooterOf, RecordPaneFooter, NowDetailPane, the lifecycle schema and dispatcher path, dropTask, dropWithChildren, close/flags/blocker rules, closingOf, record rendering, and the existing graph/supervisor/protocol/record-control tests. Queried FI3-208, FI3-206, FI3-232 and FI3-243. Public-page reads of Nielsen Norman Group's confirmation-dialog guidance, GitHub's administering-issues/closing-an-issue guide and Linear's delete-archive-issues guide support consequence-specific confirmation and the cancellation-versus-deletion distinction. git status --porcelain=v1 and git diff --stat were empty. No app run, tests or behavioral proof of an implementation are claimed.

Checkable implementation acceptance: cancel/cross dismissal produce no close event; confirm produces one captain-attributed dropped/cancelled event and a retained record; closing remains possible while blocked; named unstarted descendants cascade exactly as confirmed; closed descendants and unrelated tasks are unchanged; started descendants or concurrent start refuse without partial writes; changed effect lists require fresh confirmation; open dependents remain unready; the popover stays open with reason/time and no footer; the task leaves charted without entering done; Start, Stop it and Continue still work. Exercise keyboard focus/pending/refusal behavior, both themes and minimum window, and capture normal-footer, confirmation and retained-record images. Extend renderer footer/chrome, TaskService graph, TaskProtocol and CrewSupervisor tests plus tests/e2e/record-controls.spec.ts and now-panel.spec.ts. Update shared helpers and callers if selectors change. The build's gate is pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test, plus the relevant end-to-end specs under docs/testing.md. Update the TaskRecord design prompt/readme and code comments that currently exclude planned-task drop; do not rewrite AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

Risk
Low for this read-only proposal; the implementation must guard state and graph changes so confirmation cannot cancel newly-started or undisclosed work.

Not done

The answer card contains the source trace, diagrams, actual app pictures and proposed acceptance tests. Established: new crewmate decisions immediately place a captain gate and make Tasks wait, although presentation waits for the next report or idle boundary; a report can present a card before turn completion. Replies hide cards without removing waiting, keeps-open actions leave waiting while choices are disabled, and shown-version revisions produce errors in both directions because Tasks reads the stored head. Restart releases close-out holds but preserves unanswered replies; ordinary resolutions release gates, while another decision can keep the task waiting.

tasks.outcome:
Intent
Produced a checkable proposed specification for the ready-card fix, not an implementation. One answer card presents two directions and four numbered questions, with recommended answers and explicit assumptions. Version 1 below is the complete recommended plan; it is not yet approved. FI3-276 should build from the approved revision, not from an inferred choice.

What changed
No project files changed. Proposed specification, version 1:

1. Purpose and invariant. Waiting on you means an open or active task has a ready decision the captain can reach. It does not mean that an unresolved card was saved or that work has a captain gate. Every rendered waiting task shortcut must point at an available ready decision; notes, hidden cards, working/streaming choices and closed tasks cannot create that signal.

2. Authoritative card version. Derive eligibility from CardService.snapshot(), which includes the version the stage still shows during a pending revision. Eligible means unresolved, awaiting absent, status ready, actions nonempty, and an associated live task. Apply that same test to direct task associations and gate-backed decision/operation cards; do not use id-prefix guesses or treat any open gate reference as a decision. Keep the durable record distinct from this presentation projection.

3. Selection and reachability. Recommended Q2 answer is reachable, not foreground-only: a ready decision behind another card counts because task navigation can bring it forward. Paging does not alter task waiting. Select the first eligible associated decision in the stage's existing priority/newest order. Hidden or working cards must not mask an eligible sibling. Count each task once, however many eligible cards it has. If the selected card becomes unavailable before navigation, refresh the projection and use a remaining eligible choice or the record; never force a hidden card onto the stage.

4. Shared waiting surfaces and compatibility. Make waitingCardId the sole task waiting fact: an eligible decision id, otherwise null, including on done/dropped tasks. Use it consistently for Tasks grouping, compact waiting counts, record status/pill, decision guidance, Show the card, footer decision suppression and navigation. Preserve flags.needsYou and project counts.needsYou as broader attention facts, including existing durable-card/hold/dead-dependency cases; ready waiting must also imply attention. They no longer drive waiting labels. Add a derived project counts.waitingOnYou that counts live tasks with eligible decisions. Document this distinction for shared and personal-panel readers, update generated declarations through their generator, and update the protocol contract/version where required. No new stored task status or readiness column is needed.

5. No-card holds and controls. Captain holds, limits of tries and dropped dependency edges remain operational holds or attention, not claims that a decision is ready. The record uses existing hold/dependency information and generic attention guidance when no choice is available. Keep Start/Stop/Continue/Drop rules and host refusals intact; losing a presentation signal never releases a hold or authorizes dispatch. A blocker or interruption may remain the primary record explanation while a simultaneous eligible decision still has its Show the card route.

6. Tree behavior. Recommended Q3 answer is split: a task with a ready decision remains in Waiting on you even when its parent tree is underway. Its parent and nonwaiting siblings retain their existing grouping; do not move unrelated work into waiting or duplicate/count ancestors as decisions. Existing same-group nesting, ordering, filtering and activity indicators remain unchanged. The waiting count equals eligible tasks, not an entire tree. Alternative Q3 is nesting in Waiting with repeated, explicitly uncounted parent context; selecting it requires recording that revised layout contract before approval.

7. Existing lifecycle retained. New crewmate cards wait for report or idle/turn end, whichever comes first; a report can make a choice ready while the author continues running. Firstmate/host cards retain their current immediate presentation rules. A captain reply immediately hides its card and hands the turn to the author. An acknowledgement or unfinished write does not restore waiting; the card returns at its already-agreed release boundary after an answer. A refused reply restores the draft, card and correct signal. Keeps-open actions remove waiting while choices are Working; ready return restores it. If another eligible decision remains, waiting continues through that decision. A shown decision revised into a note remains waiting until the shown version changes; a shown note revised into a decision does not start waiting early. Silent, provider-failed and interrupted turn endings still release close-out holds. Restart still releases close-out holds and resets streaming cards to ready, while unanswered captain replies stay hidden. Stable-id reopening starts its existing new lifecycle and obeys the same eligibility rule. Dismissal/resolution removes that choice and selects any remaining eligible decision; it does not change task closure rules.

8. Updates and ordering. CardService must declare presentation changes through one generic invalidation seam, covering emission, both shown-version revision directions, reply hides, answers, close-out, streaming/ready, resolution, dismissal, withdrawal, reopening, restoration and closure. Board, already-open detail and project readers refresh even when no gate or task event would otherwise change. Advance the board revision through its existing owner so snapshot/delta application and missed-push recovery remain correct; do not directly write task tables or add fake timeline/feed progress. Coordinate card/task delivery and the immediate local reply hide so no painted waiting shortcut is ahead of its focusable card. Refusal restores the local projection; stale pushes must not resurrect a hidden signal. Assert order, not a timer delay or a wall-clock promise.

9. Recommended direction, Q1 A. Include the shared waiting fix plus the matching choice-readiness safeguard: a hidden, working or associated closed-task card cannot resolve, steer or run an effect through an action call. Refuse before those effects, preserving an open card and making the renderer distinguish refusal from acceptance rather than optimistically removing it. Valid choices still use the shown version, not a pending stored revision. This is not a redesign of submission metadata, effects, required-answer validation or action routing. Q1 B is the same complete waiting-surface fix without changing choice admission; it must not claim hidden-choice safety.

10. Scope and shipping order, Q4. Recommended answer is one cohesive ready-card change, with orphan-card retirement left to existing FI3-270. Excluding closed tasks from waiting and, in direction A, refusing their choices does not require that cleanup to merge first. If the captain chooses to include cleanup, the plan becomes two independently shippable pieces in this order: FI3-270 retires cards on cancellation/terminal failure, then the ready-card projection and surfaces. Existing separately owned work is not silently folded into FI3-276.

11. Acceptance matrix. Through real producer/consumer interfaces, assert: hidden new emission has no waiting id/group/count/status/Show the card; report while running produces a reachable ready choice; immediate reply hide and refusal restoration agree across surfaces; acknowledgement and answer-without-release stay hidden; ready return restores the signal; Working removes it; both action-changing revisions track the shown version; eligible siblings win over hidden ones; one task counts once; task navigation reaches a decision behind another card; gate-only/notes/dead dependencies/closed rows are not waiting; waiting child plus working sibling remains truthful; direct and gate-backed crewmate/Firstmate/host cards work; all relevant release and resolution boundaries preserve their existing semantics; reload/boot/reopen and snapshot/delta/gap recovery converge. Presentation-only transitions must not change dispatch, report sorting, recovery clocks or add feed/status cards. Direction A additionally proves unavailable action calls have no resolution, steer or effect and that refusal does not hide an open card in the shell.

12. Assumptions and exclusions. Retain the previously approved release and durable-gate policies rather than requiring successful turns. A ready form is waiting while the captain fills it out; incomplete required answers still block a closing submission. Count tasks rather than cards, use stage order for the shortcut, and retain existing filter/count scope outside the corrected waiting count. Do not change routing, models, accounts, signing, delivery, merge/discard permissions, notification release policy, idle recovery, activity dots or crewmate animations. FI3-271 owns activity indicators; FI3-250 owns active dependency supervision. Actual frequency in the captain's saved sessions is unknown and is not needed to define correctness.
