tasks.outcome:
Intent
Plan alpha and stable release channels without implementing or publishing anything. The selected answers remain fixed: both channels replace the same app and use the same saved-data folder; releases happen on request; stable releases also feed alpha. This report is the complete current proposed specification for FI3-280, not an implementation authorization. The card offers approval of the recommended specification or a revision with different answers.

What changed
Planning only. Research exposed two necessary refinements to FI3-269: a subscription cannot be derived solely from the installed version, because stable delivered through alpha must not unsubscribe the tester; and update notices must follow the installable channel target, not merely a release page that exists before publication finishes.

Four product questions remain, with these explicit recommended answers:
1. Channel ownership: the installed cask chooses the update subscription, remembered independently of version, with no new in-app setting. Alternative: an app-owned choice; if selected, ask in the next round where it belongs and how it guides an installation change.
2. Stable hand-off: stable is eligible for alpha, but neither channel pointer moves backwards. Example: stable 0.1.25 must not replace alpha 0.1.26-alpha.43 if the latter published first. Alternative interpretation: every stable unconditionally replaces alpha, even an older version; that requires explicit handling of an older target rather than claiming it is a newer update.
3. Returning to stable: allow an older version only when its persisted formats are supported; always refuse incompatible or unknown newer formats. Alternative: forbid every version downgrade even with identical formats.
4. An unspecified request for a release means stable, preserving today's meaning. Alternative: alpha becomes the default for operator instructions. Workflow defaults remain stable for backward compatibility regardless; operator instructions must translate the chosen meaning explicitly.

The specification below uses all four recommended answers. They are proposals until chosen; the three earlier selected answers are not reopened.

1. Installation and subscription contract
Keep Firstmate 3000.app, bundle id com.kunchenguid.firstmate3000, the existing signing identity/team, and <appData>/firstmate-3000. Keep development runs and development bundles on firstmate-3000-dev, with no migration between those roots. Provide firstmate-3000 and firstmate-3000@alpha in kunchenguid/homebrew-tap. Declare mutual conflicts, quit the existing app before replacement, and document switching by ordinary uninstall followed by install, never uninstall with saved-data deletion. Tasks, projects, sessions, sign-ins and sharing choices remain in place; preserving the signing identity avoids deliberately resetting existing grants, but real credentials must not be used in validation.

The installer owns update-channel.json under the release data root. Its closed, versioned schema records stable or alpha, for example {schemaVersion:1, channel:"alpha"}. Write it atomically after successful installation/upgrade, outside the signed bundle and without opening SQLite or migrating app data. The app reads it but does not write it. Installation of stable must overwrite an alpha marker, even when both casks carry exactly the same stable artifact/version. An alpha cask carrying a stable artifact still writes alpha. Missing, invalid or unreadable metadata falls back to alpha only for a valid alpha logical version, otherwise stable. Direct-download installs retain a valid remembered subscription; without one they use that fallback. Isolated and development runs use only their own state, never the real installed marker. Actual Homebrew support for the chosen installation-step syntax must be demonstrated, not assumed from documentation.

2. Versions and source identity
Retain one main branch and release-please for stable versioning/proposals. Ordinary merges may update a proposal but do not publish; publication follows a separately requested stable proposal merge. Alpha is a manual request from main. There is no scheduled or every-merge alpha trigger. A live alpha resolves main to one immutable source commit and derives its numeric core from the checked-out .release-please-manifest.json version plus one patch. Its logical version is X.Y.(Z+1)-alpha.N, where N is the alpha-dispatch workflow run number; gaps caused by rehearsals are acceptable. This names a preview line, not a guarantee that the next stable will use that exact patch: a breaking/minor release can sort higher.

Use private v<logical-version> tags and public firstmate-3000-alpha-v<logical-version> tags for alpha; mark alpha releases as prereleases and never the shared tap's latest release. Keep stable private vX.Y.Z and public firstmate-3000-vX.Y.Z names unchanged so already installed stable copies cannot discover alpha. Store the product source commit in publication metadata; the public tap's own tag commit is not the product source commit. Do not commit alpha versions to the manifest, package version or generated changelog. Apply the logical version only to workflow-local packaged metadata. Keep package metadata/runtime version at the full alpha version, but set both Mac bundle-version fields to its numeric core. Prove those two identities separately; do not rely on Apple accepting a prerelease suffix in a bundle field.

3. Installable update targets
Publish a small versioned firstmate-3000-updates.json on the existing public tap. It contains stable and alpha target records with logical version, release page, download URL, SHA-256 and product source commit. It is data for the existing update reader, not a new service, task runner or releases host. Validate its schema, versions and app-specific public-tap URLs. Alpha publications change only alpha. Stable publications change stable and also alpha when stable is newer than alpha's current target; equality requires consistent artifact/source identity, not a conflicting rewrite. If alpha is already newer, retain it while stable remains available in the release history. When stable advances alpha, both casks point to the same already verified stable artifact; do not build a second alpha-flavoured copy of stable.

Write target records and all applicable casks in one public-tap commit only after the public download has been fetched back without credentials and verified. Thus new update notices refer to what the cask actually supplies. Serialize publication and compare the current targets again at the write boundary, preventing late jobs from replacing newer targets. Never cancel a live publication to start another. An existing published version's bytes are immutable: retry by verifying/reusing its artifact or fail on conflicting version/source/checksum, not by clobbering it. Keep private and public records/checksum sidecars.

4. Update reader and visible behaviour
Use real prerelease-aware SemVer precedence: alpha.10 exceeds alpha.2; stable X.Y.Z exceeds X.Y.Z-alpha.N; the next numeric core exceeds both. A stable subscription considers only the stable target. An alpha subscription considers its published alpha target, which can be either an alpha or a stable artifact. Offer only a higher target under the recommended monotonic policy. Show the correct installed channel's upgrade command and the target's public release page through the existing quiet update indicator; no automatic download or installation. Add a small channel label to the existing update panel if needed to make the subscription intelligible, following the design skill rather than adding a settings screen.

Preserve the current best-effort success cache and failure behaviour. Missing target metadata during rollout permits the legacy stable release reader for stable only, filtering valid stable tags and rejecting drafts/prereleases/other products; an alpha subscription must not fabricate a target or accidentally use the stable cask command. Invalid metadata or network failure keeps the last known good result, or yields no claimed update. A valid target file missing a channel does not authorize guessing from release history. Already installed older stable binaries continue reading their existing stable prefix unchanged.

5. Saved-data safety
Before account-vault warming or normal service startup, inspect existing database migration history with a read-only connection. Reject unknown newer migrations before writable database initialization, WAL configuration, migration execution or derived-view rebuilding. Treat unrecognized newer schema as unsupported even if someone suspects its changes were additive. Track incompatible non-database persisted-format revisions explicitly too, and require future incompatible changes to advance that compatibility boundary. Release-version numbers alone do not prove data compatibility under the recommended policy.

Fresh and supported older state migrates forward normally; supported current state opens normally. An unsupported state produces a typed, plain-language startup refusal explaining that saved work was opened by a newer version and that the person should keep/reinstall a compatible alpha or await a compatible stable. It must be visible, not only logged by the process error handler. Do not start agents, alter accounts, write launch/crash counters, rewrite views, or mutate protected database/task/session data on refusal. No rollback migration, automatic backup restoration, deletion or second data folder is included.

Older shipped binaries cannot acquire this guard retroactively. The first live alpha therefore requires a separately requested, publicly verified bootstrap stable containing the guard and channel-capable reader. Record that minimum protected stable in activation instructions, and refuse live alpha publication until that protected stable is available. Rehearsals remain possible without publication. This prerequisite does not authorize the builder to cut that stable, and arbitrary installation of pre-guard historical binaries cannot be made safe by this work.

6. Verification profiles and publishing boundary
Both channels verify and package the identical pinned source commit. Alpha requires hosted Linux typecheck, check, adherence lint, unit tests and build before any signing secret is restored. The signing job retains its Mac typecheck/lint/unit checks, universal package, Developer ID signing, hardened runtime/fuses, signed-app verification, launch and release-data-root checks, notarization/stapling, final distribution-zip Gatekeeper/launch checks, checksums, private and unauthenticated public fetched-back artifact checks, and Homebrew's cask-consumer checks.

Stable additionally retains the full verify.yml Mac suite: Mac unit tests, complete hermetic Playwright journeys, installed Claude-client surface check, replay gate, development universal-package/signature/data-root/bundled-git checks. Performance-budget grading remains on request as today. Alpha deliberately omits that full Mac verification lane; this is reduced journey assurance, not reduced signing assurance. Model the requested lanes so intentional omission does not create a skipped check masquerading as green, for example a profile-driven matrix. All actual head checks on implementation PRs still require completed/success. Keep existing sleep protection and signing cleanup.

Both profiles support a publication-disabled rehearsal on an arbitrary pinned ref, including numeric bundle fields, runtime logical version and generated casks/pointers. A rehearsal creates no tag, private/public release or tap change. Its summary distinguishes omitted checks, exercised gates and unexercised live fetch-back. A real release remains a separate request after implementation.

Ordered independently shippable pieces
1. Saved-data guard and startup refusal. Touch the database boundary, startup ordering and typed refusal presentation; add supported-state, future-schema and incompatible-format tests plus an isolated visible-refusal journey. Acceptance: supported old/current state opens; unsupported state refuses without protected data mutations and shows the explanation. Existing stable distribution is unchanged. Update storage/startup documentation in this piece.
2. Durable subscription and channel-aware update notices. Add the marker reader, typed public-target consumer, correct SemVer and per-channel update panel behaviour. Acceptance: alpha.2 to alpha.10 works; matching stable is newer than alpha; stable never offers alpha; alpha receiving stable remains alpha and sees the next alpha; installing a stable marker switches to stable; invalid/offline responses do not invent updates. Legacy stable fallback keeps this piece usable before the new publication writer exists. Extend the existing shell-operations update journey and add independently runnable channel journeys; update update documentation.
3. Cask and target-generation helpers. Extend scripts/generate-cask.sh or its shared producer with typed channel/version/artifact inputs, mutual conflicts, correct public-tag URL validation, channel markers, channel caveats, and a typed target writer with monotonic advancement. Default generation remains stable. Acceptance: generate both casks, a stable artifact in the alpha cask, and the joint pointer record; real Homebrew style/installation consumers accept them in isolated state; wrong hosts/tags, invalid versions/checksums, conflicting identities and regressive targets are refused; uninstall/switch preserves the seeded saved work. Do not publish anything. Update distribution documentation.
4. Signed channel orchestration and activation runbook. Integrate the helpers with release.yml and verify.yml, immutable source/version resolution, the two lane profiles, safe publication serialization/retry, and a single cask/pointer commit. Preserve the stable release-please caller. Acceptance: publication-disabled alpha and stable rehearsals complete all their required lanes and artifact gates, prove numeric bundle and logical runtime versions, and leave both hosts/tap unchanged; a controlled publication consumer test proves alpha-only advancement, stable-to-both advancement and a late older-stable refusal to downgrade alpha. Document the separate bootstrap-stable request and first-alpha request; do not perform them as part of this build. Each piece updates every document it makes stale rather than deferring documentation to the last piece.

Complete-build acceptance
Collect product-level evidence from disposable installs/state for: (a) requesting an alpha produces only alpha-target updates through the lighter profile; (b) stable's full profile advances both when newer; (c) alpha to stable to next alpha retains alpha subscription and correct installation command; (d) switching to the stable installation restores stable-only notices while retaining seeded projects/tasks/sessions; (e) incompatible saved data visibly refuses without mutation; (f) an older stable finishing after a newer alpha does not change alpha's target; (g) rehearsals publish nothing. Actual live publication evidence is deferred to a later release request, not silently claimed by rehearsals.

Assumptions and exclusions
Stable means the more thoroughly checked channel inside today's private-alpha programme, not the public beta or a change to legal/publication gates. Keep the product repository private, the current tap/download host, macOS universal support, current Diagnostics/terms/notice promises, provider/sign-in policy and manual updating. Alpha numbering uses the next-patch rule above and increasing workflow run numbers rather than a release-please prerelease proposal. Direct downloads retain remembered subscription as specified. No new branch strategy, side-by-side app, migration between data roots, automatic updater, beta launch, telemetry dimension, rollback/restore workflow or public release is in scope. These assumptions are exposed on the card; choosing different product answers requires recording the entire revised specification before the builder proceeds.

Verified
Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, FI3-269's full research/card, and the release/versioning/packaging/update/storage/startup code and relevant documentation/tests. Inspected the pinned packaging implementation: bundleShortVersion and bundleVersion are separate from packaged metadata version. Read the Homebrew Cask Cookbook, SemVer documentation and Electron's app.getVersion documentation through read-only requests; two raw-source URLs returned 404, so no findings rely on those fetches.

Executed read-only Node probes that compiled the actual src/core/update/updateChecker.ts into memory and called its exported interface with mock HTTP responses. Current outputs: compareSemver(alpha.10, alpha.2) = 0; compareSemver(alpha.2, matching stable) = 0; an alpha-only prefixed release yields null; an alpha logical version receives no matching-stable update and gets the stable upgrade command. These reproduce the gaps the specification addresses; they are not proof of an implemented fix. Ran git status --short, git status --porcelain=v1 and git diff --stat; all showed no changes. The inspected working-copy version was 0.1.24 at 47bcb212. No files, installed apps, real data, accounts or signing/keychain material were changed. No test suite, signed rehearsal, install or publication was run because this is a read-only planning task.

Risk

Not done
No implementation, release, commit, push or pull request. The four product defaults are not yet newly agreed. Actual installer-step compatibility, signed runtime-version behaviour, notarization, isolated installation/switching and live publication must be proved by the builder/release operator as specified. No unrelated follow-up was filed; the findings above belong to this channel plan. FI3-280 must remain on request and start from the approved revision, not merely this proposal.

tasks.outcome:
Intent
The operation contract is clarified and simplified: requested choices are the input, and the confirmation output adds checked consequences/defaults rather than creating another editable draft. The captain asked, “hmm... what would be the input and output for the project-add operation then? it feels like the "draft" would simply be whatever input was passed to the tool, right?” The same card now records this correction; no implementation is authorized.

What changed
Full proposed specification, not yet agreed: retain setup_repo as the project-add boundary. Input is the existing clone/init/adopt identity shape: clone requires origin with optional name, init requires name, adopt requires path with optional name. Add optional delivery, autonomy and rigor fields using existing policy values; omit them to keep today's defaults, never to infer a new preference. The first call performs read-only validation/inspection and finishes immediately with confirmation-required, already-managed, or a refusal identifying missing/invalid input or a proved sign-in requirement. It must not call mutating setup, broadcast repo_setup, or record setup as completed while awaiting confirmation.

The confirmation-required output contains the normalized/defaulted request, independently checked consequences and a small review reference. For example, adopt ~/code/orbit with no requested settings can resolve to absolute /Users/you/code/orbit, final name orbit, detected GitHub source acme/orbit, existing history requiring no initialization, folder-stays-in-place, and defaults direct-pr/autonomy false/standard. Include final destination/fleet entry, name conflicts and relevant sign-in state where applicable. Do not invent remote history: when it cannot yet be verified, disclose conditional initial-history creation if empty. If the caller supplies every consequential field and inspection verifies it, the output largely mirrors the input; validation and the consent boundary still matter. There is one request/settings model, no independently editable draft-project model, new draft store or workflow framework. The review reference identifies the checked snapshot for approval, not another set of settings and not consent by itself.

Firstmate presents the reviewed request and facts in the existing card system. The captain edits requested policies in the form. Its Add footer action uses the existing effect-free reply-to-Firstmate route. Firstmate resumes the same operation with submitted identity/policies plus review_ref. The app verifies that the reference is linked to the actual captain footer answer and these submitted values, rechecks material identity/consequence facts, then applies setup. Model-provided confirmed=true, an echoed request, or a review reference without a real approved answer cannot authorize mutation. Normal policy edits within the displayed form are allowed; changed identity or materially changed effects require renewed checking/review. Repeated approval/retry must not create a duplicate. Successful application returns added with actual RepoView and actual setup effects; a matched already-managed adoption path or clone source returns existing RepoView without resetting policy. A same-name init collision remains a refusal, not implicit reuse.

Recommended scope remains one review before every new ordinary-project registration, including setup implied by a work request. Skip discovery and ordinary work on already-managed projects. Resolve unclear identity before dependent settings and preserve one pending review through sign-in. Local projects require no sign-in; public clones do not force it; completing sign-in does not authorize addition. The card shows final name, full source/folder, clone/link/create operation, destination, history changes, relevant sign-in facts, and all three policies. Save the selected policy before requested work starts. Recommend naming already-requested work on combined asks and using Add project and start work; an add-only request starts none. Approval grants no future merge permission beyond the selected policy.

The requested settings-style presentation is retained: divided title-and-description rows, stable-size grouped pills for pull requests/local merge and Quick/Default/Careful, and a right-anchored 36×20 Ask before merging switch with its changing state label before it. On means Asks first; off means Merges on its own. Rows wrap at narrow widths. Local merge plus Careful explains that no independent review runs. Unlike Settings' immediate saving, the form changes only pending choices. The sample starts direct-pr/asksFirst true/standard, cannot add a project, and sample adjustments are not standing-default changes.

Done criteria: all three setup modes inspect before mutation and return honest review/existing/refusal states; checked output shows normalization, effective defaults and consequences without invented facts; there is no duplicate editable draft model; pending review is not recorded as completed setup; form matches Projects controls and changes only pending choices; actual recorded approval, not caller claims, gates application; candidate selection/sign-in/cancel/close authorize no setup; stale material facts require renewed review; repeat approval/retry creates no duplicate; selected policies precede work, match Projects after reopening and survive restart; existing-folder/exact-clone-source reuse preserves policy; no new project folders, links, history, registration or requested work precedes approval.

Current verified behavior is unchanged: setup_repo accepts kind/origin/path/name, immediately calls setup and returns a text summary afterward. RepoSetupSpec/RepoSetupResult describe actual setup, not preview. Clone defaults direct-pr, init local-only, adoption follows detected origin; ordinary new projects default autonomy false/Asks first and standard/Default. GitHub receives pull requests; plain hosts receive a pushed branch. Current ambiguity/sign-in cards are not a mandatory settings review. Current operation recording treats returned setup output as settled. Card records carry offers/interactions, but no existing typed binding authorizes project setup from an approved card. The small checked-setup/recorded-answer link is therefore proposed new work, not an existing capability.

Unchanged: conversational setup/removal, app-owned clone/create locations, in-place adoption, existing defaults/policy meanings, later configuration, task overrides and personal workspace. Assumptions: the review is the input plus verified consequences; minimal checked-snapshot/approval binding is still required; Firstmate authors a normal card while the host validates structured facts, not natural language; Settings-style appearance does not imply immediate saving. Out of scope: a draft store/workflow framework, online project creation, custom clone destination, account redesign, import wizard, other feedback, implementation and shipping. FI3-292 independently owns staged-file inclusion in the initial commit; the confirmation plan is not its fix.

Verified
Re-read setup parameters/run in src/core/pi/repoTools.ts, RepoSetupSpec/RepoSetupResult and normalization/history/defaults in src/core/workspace/repoRegistry.ts, and existing card-offer/interaction storage. Earlier inspection covered operation wiring, card effects, lookup/inference, sign-in and Projects presentation. Earlier pnpm exec vitest run src/core/pi/repoTools.test.ts src/core/workspace/projectLocator.test.ts src/core/forge/projects.test.ts src/shared/rigor.test.ts passed 53 tests with scratch HOME/isolated Git/disposable data. Those tests validate current behavior, not this proposed contract, and were not rerun for the card revision. Setup/inference end-to-end journeys were read, not run; field references were GitHub Desktop clone/add-local guidance and Apple's Alerts guidance. No live accounts or user app were inspected. git status --porcelain=v1 remains clean; no files changed, commits, push or pull request.

Risk
Medium: approval binding and honest pending results are new work; removing the redundant draft model reduces complexity but does not remove the need for an enforced consent boundary.

Not done
Three product choices remain open: every first-time registration versus explicit add only (recommend every first-time); editable policy versus summary/conversational revisions (recommend editable); combined approval starts already-requested work versus add only/ask again (recommend combined). Settings-like visuals, a trigger at the project-add boundary and the corrected input-plus-verified-facts contract are recorded. Dependent questions wait for a revision; agreement is design-only.
tasks.outcome_summary: The proposal replaces the separate draft concept with the requested setup plus verified facts/defaults, and now specifies the operation's inputs and result states.

tasks.outcome:
Intent
Plan an immediate, approved, host-presented Firstmate welcome after first usable model setup. This is revision 1 of the proposed specification, not yet agreed. One card, card-e5b38248-fm-immediate-welcome-plan, contains all current questions: (1) compact orientation versus task-first copy, recommended compact orientation; (2) skip versus retain an uncreated welcome when first input wins a recovery race, recommended skip. Agreement approves the specification only, not implementation.

What changed
Nothing in the project. The complete proposed specification follows; defaults below become the agreed spec only when the captain chooses them.

Presentation and exact copy: Create one approved Firstmate-voice note titled “Welcome aboard”, with ordinary note chrome, close and reply controls, normal note priority, and no footer actions. The one-off informational introduction is explicitly allowed to remain a note despite its starter suggestion; other cards keep the ordinary decision/action rule. Do not personalize its copy with provider/account names.

Question 1, recommended compact orientation, exact paragraph order:
“Tell me what you want to do; I’ll bring back answers and choices as cards.”
“Crewmates do the work in the background and report to Activity on the left.”
“Every ask has a record in Tasks on the right.”
“Start with a project to clone, a new project, or a folder already on your Mac.”

Question 1 alternative, task-first, exact paragraph order:
“Tell me what you want to do; I’ll bring back answers and choices as cards.”
“Start with a project to clone, a new project, or a folder already on your Mac.”

Both versions follow those paragraphs with the same token-styled conceptual drawing: left box “Activity” / “Crew reports”, center accented box “Firstmate” / “Answers and choices”, right box “Tasks” / “Your asks”. Its exact caption is “These panels appear as work starts.” The drawing teaches the default layout; it does not claim empty panels are already visible, open panels, or override panel choices. The task-first version carries Activity/Tasks orientation in that drawing rather than extra paragraphs.

Timing: In the normal eligible fresh-setup path, commit the note before publishing the ready screen; present it alongside the newly enabled input. No welcome-composition inference, ordinary wake grouping, successful live answer, quiet-period wait or caption-fade completion is required. When another card is shown, keep it shown and add the welcome unread behind it. Preserve drafts, input focus, voice state, existing card priority and notification policy; do not raise a window or add a special alert. “Immediate” is an ordering/work contract, not a new guessed millisecond budget.

Usable-model eligibility: Use Firstmate’s existing local serving/preflight facts for the actual selected model, or its normal initial automatic selection, including provider role, serving account/binding, enablement and required client. Do not silently replace a pinned model or qualify merely because some unrelated account exists. A closed setup gate is insufficient because a known paused account can keep it closed. Cancelled/failed setup, no served model, disabled account, missing client and known allowance/auth pause do not create the note. Unknown allowance is not zero. No paid health probe is added and successful inference is not a prerequisite. Unexpected subsequent model/session failure remains an ordinary provider failure, not a reason to reissue the welcome. A supported local seat qualifies only for an already eligible pending setup.

Durable lifecycle: At initialization of new app data under the new behavior, persist pending eligibility only when setup initially needs a model. Fresh already-configured starts remain skipped, matching the existing no-gate-open behavior. Record skipped/consumed states durably; an in-memory open-to-closed edge is not the source of truth. Before an introduction has been created, prior captain activity, tasks, cards or a user-registered project exclude it under the recommended skip policy; the built-in personal workspace is not prior user activity. Existing installations are skipped conservatively even without an old welcome stamp. Preserve old timestamps and existing open/resolved welcome cards; never reconstruct a missing legacy welcome whose stamp meant only wake scheduling.

Reconcile pending state at boot and after account sign-in/add/remove/enablement, serving/auth/client changes, settled catalogs, typed quota pauses/recovery and local-seat changes. Startup can create the welcome when readiness changed while the app was closed. Reads and ready-state publication must not bypass reconciliation and expose a normal fresh-ready state before its committed note. Remove the new-install live-authored welcome request rather than supplementing it. Retire obsolete typed welcome inbox requests only, preserving unrelated queued work and existing legacy cards.

The proposed spec, as it stands before the captain's replies (direction A, reveal only). Rules adopted from transitions.dev's own words: closes are faster and quieter than opens and never delayed; overshoot belongs to entrances only; match on usage, never on the nearest number; every motion ships a reduced-motion guard; nothing depends on motion alone; compositor-friendly properties only. Its scale (80 to 500 ms), recipes, blur, scale and bouncy easings are not imported; the design skill's tokens stay the one vocabulary: --dur-fast 160 ms for in-place reveals, --dur-med 360 ms for a surface's entrance, --dur-slow 700 ms for dissolves, --ease-out for entrances, --ease-drift for state and bars. Triggers and motion: the shown card changes (arrival to the front, paging, a close revealing the next) fades in and rises 4 px over --dur-med, keyed by card id so a newer card restarts it, never the card's height or the pager badge; the task pane opens with opacity 0 to 1 over --dur-fast, tie and notch with it, never its top (an e2e pins that); a disclosure body (Disclosure, Projects accordion, Tasks group, record and card-body details) fades in and settles 4 px down from its header over --dur-fast, close instant and unmounting as today, height never tweened; a settings section fades in over --dur-fast and the tab label's color eases, no sliding underline; a feed line born after its document fades in opacity-only over --dur-fast, the boot snapshot and a window slide's older rows never; a reply or the working row fades in and rises 4 px over --dur-med; a frame's first draw (panel body, card body) fades from 0 to 1 over --dur-fast on onDrawn, never on a re-push or at first paint. Everything that eases today (hovers, carets, dock widths, stage lift, the Firstmate's dim and blur, the whisper, quota bars, the switch, the picture viewer) is unchanged. Closes and dismissals are instant everywhere; state commits before motion (aria, disabled, DOM on the click) and nothing waits on transitionend; entrances are keyframes on keyed nodes so an interruption restarts, never queues. tasks.outcome:
The second ask comes from losing captain authorization after the first settle attempt, not from a missing conflict-resolution instruction. The proposed full specification is below and on card-93a48623-crew-standing-merge-plan; no implementation was performed. The captain’s standing-order choice is already settled and is not being asked again.

Intent
An explicit merge click is a standing order for that task and approved pull request through legitimate conflict-only repair, not project-wide autonomy. Complete that merge without another merge-approval request once every current gate passes. Keep material changes, revocation, required reviews and existing repair allowances distinct from the merge permission.

What changed
No project files changed. This is the complete proposed specification, awaiting the card’s two choices. Agreement adopts the specification with the submitted guard and interrupt values; Review choices first requests an updated specification/card before agreement. Neither action commissions implementation.

1. Policy choices and assumptions
Question 1, guard: builder (recommended) means the builder declares repair scope with evidence; uncertainty receives an independent bounded assessment. independent means every repair additionally requires an independent, head-bound scope verdict. Both retain every existing required review; the extra assessment does not change the task’s rigor or replace its review.
Question 2, interrupt: revoke (recommended) means a non-cancelling interruption withdraws permission; Continue resumes work but cannot merge without a new click. pause means interruption suspends permission until an explicit captain Continue; restart cannot release suspension. Cancellation and the existing Stop it control always revoke, under either choice.
Explicit assumptions: the first complete release covers GitHub direct-pr tasks only; local-only merges and plain-host branches remain unchanged until later extension. Orders have no automatic expiry. Quit/restart and changes to project autonomy do not revoke a captain’s explicit order. Sign-out/lost access pauses execution, not consent. No transfer to another task, PR, repository, source/target branch or delivery method; no protection bypass or automatic increase to repair budgets. Native GitHub auto-merge/merge queues are excluded from the first release.

2. Durable authorization, separate from execution
Store a host-minted, versioned authorization on the task through TaskService: unique id/generation, captain issuer and timestamp, shown card lifecycle/offer/action/interaction ids, task/project id, GitHub host and immutable repository/PR identities, source repository/branch, target repository/branch, delivery and merge method, approved head/base and retained approved diff, accepted repair lineage, explicitly chosen child-close exception, status/reasons, and any attempt token/candidate/retry time/remote receipt. Terminal statuses distinguish consumed, revoked and invalidated; suspension is recorded when the pause policy applies. PendingSettle may remain the execution-boundary fact but must not be the permission.
Completion publication records a host-written immutable baseline on the shown offer after fresh gates. The trusted chrome click records card resolution and authorization in one database transaction, before hiding the card or external work. Approval binds to the offer actually shown, not a newer head discovered at click time. Missing/ambiguous baselines fail closed. Frame scripts and agent calls cannot grant permission or supply an actor flag that bypasses this boundary. Same interaction/double click is idempotent; another card cannot race the same task. A genuinely new approval supersedes the prior generation. Existing autonomy remains separately derived; a valid stored order permits its executor to act on the captain’s behalf even when autonomy is off. A revoked/invalidated order places a task-specific hold that ordinary project autonomy cannot silently defeat.
Do not upgrade historical failed clicks into orders. A legacy queued captain intent can migrate only with a provable exact target and approval baseline; Firstmate-origin pending settles never become captain grants.

3. Conflict recovery and scope boundary
A confirmed conflict retains the order and queues recovery to the same builder through the durable inbox. A head mismatch/409 alone does not prove a conflict. Record repair start against the accepted head and observed base. Extend the existing change-check interface, not the tool roster, with a typed repair declaration binding authorization generation, from/to heads, old/new base, operation, impact classification, changed paths, comparison evidence and validation at the repaired head. The host checks closed facts and lineage; the agent judges semantic equivalence, rather than a static diff/prose parser.
Eligible repair integrates the original approved change with newer work on the same target, preserving approved behavior; necessary compatibility edits and directly required tests/docs may qualify. Compare the last transition and the cumulative change against the original approval to prevent gradual scope drift. A renamed interface adapted without behavior change is an eligible example. New behavior/requirements, unrelated fixes including unrelated CI code repairs, feature removal/destructive choices, weakened tests/protection, changed target/delivery or unaccounted external pushes are outside authorization. Commit authorship, few changed lines or editing only conflicted files is not proof. Unknown scope gets bounded evidence gathering; it never counts as conflict-only. Material work invalidates the order and needs captain consent, with a new merge order after the final gates pass. Do not perform unapproved material work under the repair label.
Every new head is ineligible until its lineage/assessment is accepted and its fresh gates pass. Option independent adds the extra scope assessment for each transition; required app review remains independently necessary at reviewed rigor.

4. Fresh final gates
Before every attempt require a live applicable generation, exact identity/delivery, idle/no concurrent task writer, no outstanding captain guidance, allowed child/blocker state, released CI/review caps and other task holds. Re-read the pinned PR by identity: open/not draft, current source/target/head/base and merge readiness. Read all current check runs and latest statuses per context across all pages, expected required checks including ones not yet present, required GitHub reviews and applicable branch/ruleset requirements. Unknown or unsupported readiness blocks rather than using the sign-in’s bypass ability.
Every current check must be completed/success; failure, pending, skipped and neutral block. A complete zero-check read requires validation recorded at the exact final head and no missing required checks. Unreadable is never zero. A changed head invalidates old CI/local-validation evidence and required app-review evidence. Required app review must pass at the exact candidate actually reviewed: carry the pinned review head from its brief/result, not the builder’s current head when a delayed report arrives. GitHub approvals must still satisfy its current rules, including stale-approval/latest-push requirements. Required review waits keep captain consent. Retain conventional-title/commit checks and exact-head squash merge. Recheck all local holds and generation after asynchronous reads and immediately before dispatch. The remote’s effective protection remains the final safeguard; the app never bypasses it.
Existing evidenced CI repair rules, three unsuccessful-own-repair cap, one flake reservation and review cap remain. Passing CI cannot clear a captain hold. A cap may legitimately require a repair-allowance decision, but not another approval to merge the unchanged approved work. New captain-directed guidance temporarily holds execution until its impact is declared; the host does not parse natural-language intent.

5. Completion, retries and restart
Reuse SettleService, the shared supervisor tick, check watch and durable inbox rather than adding another runner. Reconcile orders on boot, idle boundaries and fresh gate facts. With accepted repair scope and all gates ready, execute the stored order automatically; Firstmate must not request a replacement completion-card merge click. Feed/task record shows approval kept, recovery, holds, withdrawal and success; no progress/CI-wait cards. An authorization flag alone is not a moving-work witness: the idle ladder must still detect missing continuations and stalls.
Retain per-task exclusion through cleanup. Persist a durable attempt token bound to generation and exact candidate before dispatch; dedupe continuations/repair wakes by generation and head/base. Existing short transient backoff may continue, then use persisted delayed reconciliation instead of restart-reset hot loops. Conflict, sign-in, permission and protection refusals wait for recovery/new facts; ordinary CI observations never spend repair attempts.
Before retrying a timeout or recovering an in-flight crash, query the pinned PR including closed/merged state. Validate actual merge success/receipt; do not equate a successful HTTP call or an absent open PR with merging. Already merged means consume the order and finish local close/cleanup once, not merge again. An uncertain outcome remains recorded and is investigated/read again; retry only after proving the exact PR still open/unmerged and re-running all gates. Local closure and worktree retirement keep existing one-writer/purge semantics.

6. Revocation and race boundary
Provide typed per-task withdrawal through the existing task-update interface, preserving work. Cancel/discard/supersession revokes before asynchronous teardown; unregister/repository identity changes or changed target/delivery invalidates. Do not copy permission to a replacement task, and do not broaden an old proceed-with-open exception to newly introduced children. An autonomy-default change alone cannot reinterpret explicit consent. A plain card dismissal before approval grants nothing; the approved card disappearing afterwards is not revocation.
Revocation advances the generation, cancels unsent continuations and is checked after every await and immediately before remote dispatch. A stale wake cannot revive it. If dispatch already occurred, freeze further merge attempts and reconcile the remote outcome before PR closure/teardown races it. Report accepted merges as merged, even if cancellation arrived too late; never promise an already-sent merge was undone. Non-cancelling interrupt follows the selected revoke/pause policy. App quit itself is not a captain interruption.

7. Minimal complete shipping pieces
Piece 1: authorization/offer-baseline transaction, idempotency, revocation and fresh same-head final gates.
Piece 2: repair declarations/lineage and semantic assessment, exact-head reviews, complete paginated checks and merge readiness, plus Firstmate/both-backend recovery instructions.
Piece 3: durable attempt/retry/result reconciliation, task-record visibility, one-click integration/e2e coverage and affected documentation/contracts. All three are required before advertising the requested behavior; the first piece alone must not auto-adopt changed heads.

8. Acceptance and safety tests
Through real footer/IPC and a disposable GitHub stand-in, autonomy off: one click, conflict, confined repair, changed head with pending CI, current checks and required reviews pass, exactly one successful merge/task close and no second merge-approval card. Exercise both model backends. Required app review at an old head or a delayed verdict must not bless the repaired head; stale/missing required GitHub approvals hold. Assert refusal for cumulative drift/material changes, unexplained pushes, missing/unknown evidence, wrong task/PR/repository/source/target/delivery, and fabricated agent/frame authority. Cover every non-success check, more than one page of checks, missing expected jobs, unknown readiness, protected-branch refusal, both caps and green arriving during a captain hold. Cover duplicate clicks/cards, superseded generations, stale wakes and head races. Inject crashes before/after the click transaction, during repair/check/review waits, after dispatch before response and after remote success before local close. Revoke/interrupt/cancel/discard before dispatch, during a gate read and during an ambiguous request; old wakes never restore consent and too-late cancellation is honest. Access recovery retains consent but refreshes gates; complete zero checks works only with final-head local evidence. Preserve ordinary local/plain-host, answer and personal-workspace paths.

Verified
Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md first, then traced completion actions/gates and CrewSupervisor.act → CardService.resolve → SettleService.reportCardSettle/settleTaskGuarded/autonomyRefusal. pendingSettle is persisted only while waiting for a working turn and cleared in finally after an attempt; recovery’s Firstmate merge is again refused by autonomy-off. prCi.ts already does a fresh all-check gate and typed transient retries; GitHubForge already sends the exact-head guard. Its open-only branch lookup, single-page check reads and absent required-review readiness need extending for this specification. settleReview currently derives the head at report handling; final settle lacks an exact-review-head/cap preflight of its own. Existing checkWatch, InboxStore, TaskService and offer/interaction evidence supply reusable persistence seams.
Inspected, not executed: crewSupervisor.test.ts’s receipt/duplicate/mid-turn/restart cases; prCi.test.ts’s gates/retries/caps; githubForge.test.ts; tests/e2e/settle-effects.spec.ts’s real click/merge and stale-head refusals. Read docs/forge.md, delivery-rigor.md, task-record.md, inbox.md and the design system. Fetched public GitHub Docs on auto-merge and branch protection, the public REST merge API description, and Git’s range-diff documentation without sign-in. Native auto-merge can survive writer pushes and enforces required checks rather than this app’s stricter all-current-checks rule, so it is insufficient alone. GitHub updates can dismiss reviews; range-diff is recommended comparison evidence but explicitly not machine-stable parser output.
Read-only commands included git status --short, git status --porcelain=v1, git diff --stat and git log -1; status/diff were clean at inspected commit 139d9ad5. Source searches/file reads and in-memory public-document retrieval made no changes. No tests/builds or real-account operations ran. The card’s figures show lost authorization, the two assessment directions and the hold/revocation boundary; they are explanatory diagrams, not implemented-product evidence.

Local/plain-host durable orders and native auto-merge/merge queues are deliberately outside the first release. The separate manually merged PR/task-closure gap already has owner FI3-213; no duplicate follow-up was filed, and this proposal requires pinned outcome reconciliation specifically for its own attempts.

Attach current named settings to author-directed replies through the existing generic form/reply seam so feedback or “build as adjusted” cannot silently use an old snapshot. This is a proposed transport correction, not behavior already implemented; control changes must not start author turns.

Established original findings remain: FI3-298 offered capture plus default Finish exploring; its chosen finish action submitted unchanged settings, but its report required another build ask. Firstmate later relayed explicit shipping permission. FI3-299’s audited original footer offered capture plus default Keep this prototype without a recorded closing choice. tasks.outcome:
Intent
Finish the custom-provider specification without implementation, preserving the captain’s eight selections. The existing Review these choices was intermediate, not final acceptance.

What changed
No files changed. One round 2 decision card records the complete revised specification below. Two consequential questions remain: Q9 recommends allowing explicitly approved organization CA certificates for one private-HTTPS connection only (certs=scoped), rather than only the request transport’s normal trusted roots (certs=standard); Q10 recommends requiring store:false on every Responses request and refusing servers that reject it (retention=strict), rather than allowing omission only after explicit per-connection consent to possible server retention (retention=consent). Neither recommendation is yet accepted. After Review these choices, revise the same card and report the full specification with the selections before final acceptance. Final acceptance hands directly to existing FI3-328, without another build approval or a replacement implementation task.

Full revised specification
1. Preserved decisions: scope=gateway; entry=both; models=manual; save=paused; roles=both; storage=private; address=new; disconnect=stop. Gateway scope inherits local HTTP/HTTPS and explicit local no-key support from the earlier option; it also includes public HTTPS, private-network HTTPS and explicitly chosen Chat Completions or Responses. Keyless remains local-only; private-network HTTPS requires a Bearer [redacted] Both entry points are Intelligence → Add account and first setup. Welcome-card presentation remains separate.

2. Ownership and setup: one named connection owns an app-generated provider identity, one account and isolated credentials/configuration. Names, addresses and model IDs never become filesystem paths; duplicate addresses and IDs remain isolated. Reuse AccountVault/account backend, the Pi boundary, SessionFactory, model board and existing account actions; do not repoint built-in providers or rewrite the person’s custom configuration. Setup collects label, absolute API base, explicit network mode and protocol, masked key or local no-key, manual/listed models and documented limits. Show canonical full destination before any request and disclose key/content exposure, crewmate authority on the Mac, possible charges and retention. A paused saved draft sends no discovery or model requests until explicitly checked. Launch, Settings and account actions never await discovery.

3. URL contract: trim outer URL whitespace, canonicalize host/port, remove trailing slashes, preserve base path and never invent /v1. Reject embedded credentials, queries, fragments, unsupported schemes, ambiguous encodings and disguised numeric loopback forms. Reject operation URLs ending /models, /responses or /chat/completions, offering a base suggestion for explicit confirmation. A changed host, port or base path creates a new connection with fresh key, trust, check and use choices; the original remains until explicitly removed and never forwards its key.

4. Network contract: public mode permits publicly routed HTTPS. Explicit private mode permits private/VPN-network HTTPS, including RFC1918, IPv6 unique-local and shared-address VPN ranges, with a key. Local mode permits only localhost, canonical 127.0.0.1 and [::1]; localhost must resolve/connect only to loopback. Local HTTP needs an unencrypted-local warning; no-key sends no Authorization header or placeholder. Refuse link-local, unspecified, multicast, reserved/non-service and known metadata-service destinations regardless of mode. A shared guard covers discovery, checks, inference, compaction, retries and background model requests. Validate IPv4, IPv6 and mapped addresses on each new connection; refuse disallowed/mixed-mode DNS answers and pin the validated address for that request while preserving hostname verification. Later connections may resolve anew within the approved class but cannot silently cross classes. Reject every redirect, including same-host redirects, alternate endpoints/auth flows/executable configuration and automatic server-link opening. No ambient proxy bypass; ordinary network/VPN may carry a direct connection, but this feature adds no authenticated proxy setup. Unknown internal services cannot all be recognized by IP, so endpoint consent is not a hostile-server defense.

5. Certificate decision Q9: standard uses the actual request transport’s normal trusted roots and does not promise recognition of every certificate installed on macOS. Scoped additionally allows locally supplied, bounded PEM CA certificates only on a private-HTTPS connection, with explicit identity/fingerprint review and consent. Public certificate material belongs to the account; never import private keys, download certificates, modify global trust, support client-certificate authentication or disable hostname/chain/expiry validation. Apply the CA only in that connection’s transport. Removal/replacement invalidates proof; test a candidate trust revision before replacing a working revision. Validate this in the packaged transport because Electron/Node trust behavior cannot be assumed identical.

6. Credential contract: one typed Settings submission sends the masked key to the credential owner as opaque literal data, never command/environment interpolation or another credential reference. Reject values not safely representable in a Bearer [redacted]; never fall back to ambient or built-in credentials. The saved key never returns to account views, agents, cards or feeds; expose key-present state only. Clear input on completion/cancel. No keys in persistent UI state, database settings, model definitions, process arguments or child environments. Preserve selected app-private, unencrypted storage using 0700 directories and 0600 auth files. A local availability placeholder must never become a Bearer [redacted]

7. Protocol/profile contract: choose openai-completions (Chat Completions, not legacy text completions) or openai-responses explicitly per connection; never probe/fall back between them automatically. Both require streamed text, finalized valid function-call arguments, matching tool results and another completed text response. Start text-only with reasoning controls off, ordinary system instructions/function tools, no developer-only or strict-schema assumption, grammar tools, hosted tools or tool search. Omit optional sampling/service-tier fields and affinity identifiers. Use explicit tested profiles rather than URL heuristics; profile changes invalidate proof. Chat requires terminal finish_reason and a tested bounded-output field; optional usage reporting may be omitted, with absent usage unknown. Responses requires stream:true, max_output_tokens and completed terminal events; reject truncated, malformed, failed or unexpectedly queued replies. Replay needed input locally; do not use previous_response_id, server conversation objects, polling, WebSocket continuation or remote response retrieval. Required safety fields cannot be removed as speculative compatibility fallback. No arbitrary header/payload/profile editor.

8. Responses storage decision Q10: strict requires store:false for checks and every other Responses request; a rejecting server is incompatible, with no silent retry omitting the field. Consent keeps strict as the default but permits field omission on an explicitly consented connection revision after warning that server defaults may retain responses. Never send store:true or silently downgrade. The check uses the exact saved policy; a policy change invalidates proof and requires new consent/check. Neither alternative depends on server-saved continuation. Disable custom cache warming and explicit cache retention for all request paths, sending no cache key/retention fields or internal session-affinity identifiers. This cannot prevent implicit server caching/logging. store:false is a request, not a privacy guarantee, and is separate from app-private key storage.

9. Models and limits: optionally read bounded GET {base}/models after consent, while preserving manual IDs even when listing fails. Deduplicate/render IDs as text and ignore server-supplied endpoints, headers, executable settings, unverified capabilities/prices. Require documented positive integer context/output limits with output below context; unknown limits block activation rather than inventing defaults. Check each model/configuration separately. Failed listing retains choices and last successful metadata, never proving a departure. Enforce declared input/output envelopes including tools and instructions; estimates cannot prove absence of server-side truncation. Unknown allowance, usage and price never mean zero or free. Connection-owned definitions do not fetch custom metadata from Pi’s public catalog; built-in catalog behavior remains intact.

10. Functional check: disclose possible charges; use fixed synthetic instructions and a harmless in-memory echo tool, never project files/history, the Firstmate prompt or real work tools. Assert expected tool name/arguments, matching synthetic result and completed streamed text; execute no other returned action. Proposed bounds: listing 15 seconds, 1 MiB and 1,000 IDs; two generation requests within 60 seconds total, at most 128 output tokens and 1 MiB reply each, no automatic retry. Cancellation aborts and blocks late activation. Proof binds canonical address/network mode, credential revision, model/limits/profile, protocol, certificate revision and storage policy. Relevant changes invalidate it.

11. State/use contract: distinguish saved/untested, checking, checked, selected/ready, paused, unreachable, rejected key and incompatible. A passing check establishes interoperability, not model quality. Firstmate selection is explicit, changing only at the existing idle boundary; crew use requires slot placement or an explicit named-model request. Unchecked/paused/unplaced custom models cannot enter all-model automatic fallbacks or background decisions. Background decisions may use an explicitly crew-eligible checked model under the same transport policy. First setup stays closed until a checked model is explicitly chosen for Firstmate; save-paused or crew-only selection cannot open it. Preserve built-in model choices/routing/quota honesty.

12. Save/lifecycle contract: failed/cancelled setup changes nothing unless explicitly saved paused. Rename preserves identity/choices. Pause blocks new requests without deleting the key and does not silently cancel the current turn; Resume requires valid proof. Same-address key replacement tests the candidate before idle-boundary switching; failure/cancel preserves the working credential and a paused candidate cannot replace it. Protocol/profile/limit revisions invalidate matching proof without changing an active turn mid-request. Address changes use the selected new-connection rule. Disconnect warns of active-work/Firstmate consequences, immediately blocks new requests, stops matching turns and their owned background jobs, settles in-flight writes/cached runtimes, then removes only this connection’s credentials, certificates, metadata and caches. Late callbacks cannot recreate files or reactivate it. Preserve task/session history and sibling accounts; retire references without silently moving Firstmate/stopped work to another server. Local deletion does not revoke the server key, retract sent content or delete server logs.

13. Errors/security: translate untrusted failures before logs/session persistence, not only on display. Keep bounded allowlisted categories/status/safe request identifiers, discard raw bodies/headers/links, and remove exact keys and ordinary escaped echoes. A 401 is API-key rejection requiring key review, with no renewal; 403 is access refusal, not automatically a bad key. Distinguish path/model, tools/stream, rate-limit, TLS/trust, network, malformed/oversized and timeout categories. Redaction cannot contain a hostile server disguising secrets in generated content or misusing received data; trusted operator/model remains a prerequisite.

14. Acceptance and implementation order: first guarded transport, literal credentials and safe errors; then complete account/check/model/lifecycle journey, followed by local/private modes and Responses under the same guard. All selected scope is required before feature completion; a partial key form is not shippable. With disposable app state/local fixture servers/synthetic keys prove both entry points, all modes/protocols, selected Firstmate card and crew task destination, manual recovery, save-paused/restart, explicit routing and first-setup gating, duplicate connection isolation, multi-turn/tool replay and compaction. Exercise cancellation, partial/malformed/oversized streams, 401 vs 403, rate limits and offline recovery. Unsafe URLs/redirects/rebinding/mapped addresses/mixed network modes/known metadata/alternate destinations fail before transmission there; no-key has no Authorization; cache/session identifiers are absent on all custom paths. Standard cert mode refuses unrecognized roots; scoped additionally proves isolated roots, correct name/expiry/chain, no sibling or built-in trust spill, revision invalidation and restart/removal. Strict storage proves store:false on every Responses path and visible rejection; consent proves no omission before per-connection consent, persistence and exact-policy checks, and no automatic downgrade. Verify failed replacement preserves the working revision, Pause blocks new use, Disconnect stops matching work with no late recreation/sibling deletion, literal command-looking keys cannot execute, and opaque-key error echoes are absent from settings/model files/account responses/logs/sessions/cards/feeds/exports. Run the repository green gate and affected account/first-setup/model/routing/session end-to-end journeys plus new adversarial fixtures. Update architecture outbound-network policy and account/model/first-setup/design documentation with implementation.

15. Assumptions and exclusions: macOS desktop, a direct compatible endpoint reachable via normal networking/VPN, Bearer [redacted] except explicit local no-key, trusted server/model, documented limits and no generic allowance API. Private permission is explicitly selected, never inferred from hostname. No private-network HTTP, TLS bypass/global trust changes, mutual TLS/private signing keys, OAuth/non-Bearer [redacted], Azure-specific query/version conventions, arbitrary headers/payloads, automatic reasoning/vision/protocol detection, embeddings/image generation, executable imports, installation/downloads, automatic server-saved continuation, key revocation or machine isolation. Generic local support does not inherit development-only Ollama safeguards or loosen that gate. Implementation belongs to FI3-328 after final acceptance; no implementation is authorized by this round’s Review action.

Verified
Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; FI3-327/FI3-328 records; docs/architecture.md, docs/model-lists.md and docs/subscriptions-tab.md; src/core/pi/accountVault.ts, piAccountBackend.ts, modelRuntime.ts and session.ts; src/shared/providers.ts; pinned Pi 0.99.1 models/custom-provider docs and installed Responses request/conversion/stream code. Ran two stdin-only attempts of `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$PWD/.unused-research-home" FM3000_LOCAL_CODESIGN_DIR="$PWD/.unused-research-home/signing" PI_OFFLINE=1 node --input-type=module`, with injected fetch and a global real-network refusal. The first probe assertion incorrectly expected cross-model ID normalization for same-model replay; inspection corrected it to assert matching actual call/result IDs, and the corrected probe passed. It exercised real driver streamed tool arguments, synthetic result, final text, /proxy/v1/responses path, store:false, full local replay without continuation, max_output_tokens, suppressed identifiers under cacheRetention:none, identifiers sent under default short caching, missing-terminal-event refusal and default redirect=follow. A non-exported package-version lookup failed; direct package-file reading confirmed 0.99.1. Final `git diff --stat` and `git status --short` were empty at 4ebfa085; `test ! -e .unused-research-home` passed. No files or scratch HOME created, real network, real account/credential/keychain/signing material, install, commit, push or PR. No app test suite was needed for this answer-only research; the finished UI, guards and real/private certificate transport are not verified yet.

Risk
Medium: expanded network reach and server trust expose credentials/project content and allow model-directed work; scoped certificates and explicit storage requests reduce specific risks but cannot make a hostile server safe.

Not done
No implementation or final acceptance. Await Q9/Q10, then revise this same card and report the full selected specification for final plan acceptance; that acceptance directly hands to FI3-328. No additional task filed. Welcome presentation remains separately planned.
