tasks.outcome:
Intent
Consolidate FI3-327 and FI3-334 into the complete custom API/gateway implementation specification, preserving the captain’s selections. Review these choices is intermediate, not final implementation acceptance.

What changed
No files changed. One final decision card records the specification below, with Accept and implement as the recommended default and Revise the plan as the alternative. There are no remaining dependent product questions. Final acceptance directly authorizes existing builder FI3-328; do not create another builder or ask for redundant build permission. Until that acceptance, implementation remains unauthorized.

Full specification
1. Preserved selections and ownership: scope=gateway, entry=both, models=manual, save=paused, roles=both, storage=private, address=new, disconnect=stop, certs=scoped, retention=consent. Gateway scope includes public HTTPS, local HTTP/HTTPS with explicit local no-key support, private-network HTTPS with a Bearer [redacted], and explicitly chosen Chat Completions or Responses. One named connection owns an app-generated provider identity, one account and isolated configuration/credentials. Names, addresses and model IDs never become filesystem paths. Duplicate addresses and model IDs remain isolated. Reuse AccountVault/account backend, the Pi boundary, the existing runtime factory, SessionFactory, model board and account actions; do not repoint built-in providers or rewrite the person’s custom configuration.

2. Setup and consent: Intelligence → Add account and first setup use the same Custom API flow. Collect label, absolute API base, explicit network mode/protocol, masked Bearer [redacted] or local no-key, model IDs and documented limits. Show canonical full destination before any request. Disclose credential/content exposure, model-directed work on this Mac, possible charges and retention. Organization certificates and the storage exception require separate connection-specific approvals. Saving paused sends no discovery or generation requests. Launch, Settings, account creation and routing never wait on discovery. Welcome-card presentation is separate work.

3. Address contract: trim outer URL whitespace, canonicalize host/port, remove trailing slashes, preserve base path and never invent /v1. Reject embedded credentials, queries, fragments, unsupported schemes, ambiguous encodings and disguised numeric loopback spellings. Refuse operation URLs ending /models, /responses or /chat/completions, offering a base suggestion for explicit confirmation. Changing canonical host, port or base path creates a separate connection with fresh key entry, destination/certificate/storage approval, checks and use choices. The original remains until explicitly removed and never forwards its key.

4. Network contract: public mode permits publicly routed HTTPS. Explicit private mode permits private/VPN HTTPS with a key, including private IPv4, IPv6 unique-local and shared-address VPN ranges. Local mode permits only localhost, canonical 127.0.0.1 and [::1]; localhost must resolve/connect only to loopback. Local HTTP requires an unencrypted-local warning. Local no-key sends no Authorization header or availability placeholder. Refuse link-local, unspecified, multicast, reserved/non-service and known metadata-service destinations in all modes. One guarded transport covers listing, checks, inference, compaction, retries and background model requests. Validate IPv4/IPv6/mapped addresses on every new connection, refuse disallowed/mixed-mode DNS results, and pin the validated address for that request while retaining hostname verification. Later resolutions may move within the approved class, never silently cross classes. Reject every redirect, including same-host, alternate endpoints/auth flows/executable configuration and automatic server-link opening. No ambient proxy bypass or additional authenticated-proxy setup; normal networking/VPN may carry direct connections. Bound response sizes. Unknown internal services cannot all be recognized by IP; endpoint approval does not make a hostile server safe.

5. Selected certificate policy: use the actual request transport’s normal roots, additionally permitting locally supplied, bounded PEM CA certificates only for an explicitly approved private-HTTPS connection. Review certificate identity/fingerprint before consent; persist public certificate material under that account and apply it only to its transport. Reject private keys, remote certificate downloads and client-certificate authentication. Keep hostname, chain and expiry validation; never modify global trust or ignore certificate errors. Removal/replacement invalidates affected proof. Test candidate trust before replacing a working revision. Prove isolation, restart and validation in the packaged transport; do not assume Electron, Node and macOS share trust behavior or that every Mac-installed certificate is recognized.

6. Credential contract: a typed Settings submission sends the masked key once to the credential owner as opaque literal data, never command/environment interpolation or another credential reference. Reject values not safely representable in a Bearer [redacted] No ambient/built-in credential fallback. Clear input on completion/cancel; account views return key-present state, never the saved key. No keys in persistent UI state, database settings, model definitions, process arguments, child environments, agents, cards, feeds or exports. Selected app-private storage is unencrypted, using 0700 directories and 0600 auth files. An internal local no-key availability marker must never become a Bearer [redacted]

7. Protocol/profile contract: select openai-completions, meaning Chat Completions rather than legacy text completions, or openai-responses explicitly per connection. Never auto-probe or fall back between them. Both require streamed text, finalized valid ordinary function calls, paired matching tool results and another completed text response. Use explicit tested minimal profiles rather than URL heuristics: text-only, reasoning controls off, plain system instructions, no developer-only/strict-schema assumption, grammar/hosted tools or tool search. Omit optional sampling/service-tier fields and session-affinity identifiers. Chat requires terminal finish reason and a tested bounded-output field; optional usage reporting may be omitted and absent usage is unknown. Responses requires stream:true, max_output_tokens and completed terminal events; refuse truncated, failed, malformed or unexpectedly queued replies. Replay needed history locally; no previous_response_id, server conversation objects, polling, WebSocket continuation or remote response retrieval. Required safety fields cannot be weakened for compatibility. No arbitrary header/payload/profile editor.

8. Selected Responses storage contract: default every Responses request to store:false. A rejecting server stops with an incompatibility explanation; never silently retry omitting the field. A default-off optional setting may omit it only after explicit consent to possible server retention for that connection. Approval binds the connection’s policy revision and persists across restart; never send store:true. Check exactly the saved policy. Changing policy invalidates proof and requires a new check; enabling or changing the exception requires fresh consent. New connections never inherit approval. Neither mode uses server-saved continuation. Disable custom cache warming and explicit cache retention; send no cache keys, cache-retention fields or internal affinity identifiers on checks, turns, compaction or background paths. This cannot stop implicit server logging/caching. store:false is a request, not a privacy guarantee; server retention is separate from local key storage.

9. Safe failures: translate untrusted provider errors at the request boundary before logging or session persistence. Preserve bounded allowlisted categories/status and safe request identifiers, discard raw bodies/headers/links and remove exact keys and ordinary escaped echoes. A 401 requests key review/replacement with no API-key renewal; 403 is access refusal, not automatically a bad key. Distinguish wrong path/model, tools/streaming incompatibility, rate limit, certificate/trust, network, malformed/oversized reply and timeout, with safe Retry/Edit recovery. A malicious server can disguise secrets in generated content or misuse received data; filtering does not make it trustworthy.

10. Models and limits: after consent, optionally read bounded GET {base}/models. Manual IDs remain available when listing fails or is unsupported. Deduplicate/render IDs as text; ignore supplied endpoints, headers, executable settings and unverified capability/price claims. Require documented positive integer context/output limits with output below context; unknown limits block activation rather than inventing defaults. Check each model/configuration separately. Failed listing preserves saved choices and last successful metadata, never proving departure. Enforce declared request envelopes including instructions, history and tools; estimates cannot prove absence of server truncation. Unknown allowance, usage and price never mean zero/free. Connection-owned model definitions do not fetch custom metadata from Pi’s public catalog; built-in catalog behavior remains intact.

11. Functional check/proof: disclose possible charges. Use fixed synthetic instructions and one harmless in-memory echo tool, never project files/history, Firstmate prompts or real work tools. Assert expected tool name/arguments, matching synthetic result and completed streamed text; execute no other returned action. Defaults are listing within 15 seconds, 1 MiB and 1,000 IDs, and two generation requests within 60 seconds total, each at most 128 output tokens or the smaller documented limit and 1 MiB response, without automatic retries. Cancellation aborts and prevents late activation. Bind proof to canonical address/network mode, credential revision, model/limits/profile, protocol, certificate revision and storage policy; relevant changes invalidate it. This establishes interoperability, not model quality, capacity or trustworthiness.

12. State/use contract: distinguish saved/untested, checking, checked, selected/ready, paused, unreachable, rejected key and incompatible. Firstmate selection is explicit and rebinds only at the existing idle boundary. Crew use requires slot placement or an explicit named-model request. Unchecked, paused and unplaced custom models cannot enter automatic pool fallbacks or background decisions. Explicitly crew-eligible checked models may serve background decisions only under the same guard. On first setup, paused save or crew-only selection cannot open the ready screen; custom use requires a checked model explicitly chosen for Firstmate. Readiness derives from existing state, not a new first-run flag. Preserve built-in choices and routing/quota rules.

13. Save/lifecycle contract: failure/cancel changes nothing unless explicitly saved paused. Rename preserves identity/choices. Pause blocks new use without deleting the key: an already in-flight request may finish, but subsequent model requests wait for Resume rather than silently cancelling or migrating the turn. Resume requires valid proof. This reconciles the earlier block-new-requests and do-not-silently-cancel language without another product fork. Same-address key replacement is transactional: check candidate, switch at idle, preserve the working revision on failure/cancel; a paused candidate cannot replace it. Protocol/profile/limit changes invalidate matching proof and never alter an active request mid-flight. Address changes follow the new-connection rule. Disconnect warns about active-work/Firstmate consequences, immediately blocks new requests, stops matching turns and their owned background jobs, settles pending writes/cached runtimes, then removes only this connection’s credentials, certificates, metadata and caches. Late callbacks cannot recreate files or reactivate it. Preserve task/session history and sibling accounts; retire references without silently moving Firstmate or stopped work to another server. Local deletion cannot revoke a server-issued key, retract transmitted data or erase server logs.

Done checks and required evidence for FI3-328
A. With disposable app state, isolated fixture servers and synthetic keys, exercise both entry points, all selected network modes and both protocols. A Firstmate card and crew task must reach only their explicitly selected address/model. Demonstrate manual-model recovery, refusal of unknown limits, paused save/restart with zero requests, explicit selection, first-setup gating and duplicate address/ID isolation. Existing accounts and model choices remain unchanged.
B. Capture actual wire requests through multi-turn/tool replay, compaction and background consumers. Exercise cancellation, partial/malformed/oversized/missing-terminal streams, 401 versus 403, offline/timeout/rate-limit recovery. Unsafe URLs, redirects, rebinding, mapped/mixed-mode resolutions, metadata and alternate destinations fail before credentials/content reach a refused destination. Local no-key sends no Authorization. Custom cache/session identifiers are absent on every path. Fixtures use test seams without loosening production policy.
C. In the packaged transport, prove scoped CA acceptance only for its approved connection, wrong-name/expired/untrusted refusal, no sibling/built-in trust spill, revision invalidation, restart and removal. Every default Responses path sends store:false; rejection never causes automatic omission. Prove no omission without connection-specific consent, exact-policy checks, persisted approval, change invalidation and no inheritance by new connections. Neither mode depends on remote continuation.
D. Failed/cancelled replacement preserves the working revision. Pause prevents subsequent requests. Disconnect stops matching work without late recreation, sibling deletion or silent migration. Command/environment-looking keys remain literal and cannot execute. An opaque synthetic key echoed by hostile error fixtures is absent from account responses, settings/model files, logs, sessions, cards, feeds and exports. Exercise interfaces and persisted behavior, not source-string assertions.
E. Run pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence && pnpm test, the affected account/first-setup/model/routing/session end-to-end journeys and new custom-connection/adversarial fixtures. Existing starting points include tests/e2e/first-launch.spec.ts, subscriptions-instruments.spec.ts, model-lists.spec.ts and card-action-feedback.spec.ts; trace additional callers of changed shared contracts. Run pnpm replay:gate when repository triggers apply. Use hermetic HOME/userData and mock providers, never real accounts/keychains. Update architecture outbound-network policy and account/model/first-setup/design documentation. Record screenshots, request transcripts and safe persisted state as product evidence. A partial key form or unguarded request path is not complete.

Shippable pieces
P1: independently tested guarded transport, literal credentials and safe errors without new UI. P2: complete public-HTTPS Chat Completions account/check/model/select/restart/lifecycle journey. P3: local HTTP/HTTPS/no-key and private HTTPS with scoped certificates under the same guards. P4: Responses with local replay, default no-save requests and consented server-storage-default exception across every consumer. Pieces may be reviewed and merged separately; all selected scope and done checks are required for feature completion.

Assumptions
macOS desktop; direct compatible endpoint reachable through normal networking/VPN; Bearer [redacted] except explicit local no-key; trusted operator/model; documented limits; no generic allowance API. Private permission is explicit, never inferred from a hostname. The check bounds are implementation limits, not proof of server capacity. Pause allows an in-flight request to finish but gates later requests; Disconnect stops work. Final acceptance approves documenting the custom-destination exception to current outbound policy, not unrestricted network access.

Exclusions
No private-network HTTP, certificate bypass/global trust edits, mutual TLS/client private keys, OAuth/non-Bearer [redacted], Azure-specific query/version conventions, arbitrary headers/payload editors, automatic protocol/vision/reasoning detection, embeddings/image generation, executable imports, server installation/downloads, server-saved continuation, key revocation, machine isolation, guaranteed server non-truncation or retention enforcement. Generic local compatibility does not inherit development-only Ollama safeguards or loosen that gate. Welcome-card presentation and separate account-choice work remain outside this feature, as in earlier planning.

Verified
Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the design skill; full FI3-327/FI3-334 reports and cards; FI3-326/FI3-328 records; docs/model-lists.md, docs/subscriptions-tab.md and docs/first-launch.md; relevant architecture policy sections and accountVault.ts; modelRuntime.ts and src/shared/providers.ts. This confirms existing account-owner/runtime seams, catalog-gated account creation and the routing/first-setup contracts the builder must extend. Prior synthetic driver probes are inherited research, not tests rerun here or finished-feature proof. Ran git status --short, git rev-parse --short HEAD, git diff --stat, git log -1 --format='%h %s' and test ! -e .unused-research-home; all succeeded, diff/status were empty at 4ebfa085 and the prior scratch HOME was absent. Listed existing end-to-end specs to identify validation starting points. No app tests or network requests, real credentials/accounts/keychains/signing access, files changed, commit, push or pull request. The proposed UI, transport guard and packaged certificate isolation are not implemented or verified yet.

Risk
Medium: expanded network reach exposes credentials/project content and permits model-directed work; scoped certificates and explicit retention consent reduce specific risks but cannot make a hostile server safe.

Not done
Implementation and final acceptance. The card asks for final Accept and implement now; that acceptance starts existing FI3-328 directly from this full specification, without another permission question. No additional task filed.

tasks.outcome:
Intent
FI3-363: while an e2e run of a working copy is launching apps from out/, a `pnpm build` there (including `pnpm test:e2e`'s build step) must wait or be refused. I chose refusal: it answers at once, while a wait could block a builder's command for a whole e2e run.

What changed
- **The guard.** `scripts/refuse-build-during-e2e.ts` is now the first step of `prebuild`. While a run of the working copy is going it exits 1 before anything is written, with one message naming the run (`test-results/runs/<run>/` and the runner's pid) and what to do instead.
- **The live-run check.** `liveRuns` in `tests/e2e/runEvidence.ts` reads FI3-346's per-run directories, so there is no new lock. A run counts as going only while a process with its pid is running and started no later than the run's named start (read with `ps -o etime=`), so a reused pid never blocks a build. The evidence tidy-up now uses the same check.
- **Docs.** `docs/testing.md` explains the refusal, and `docs/test-cohorts.md` records the new test case's timing.

Verified
- **Real transcripts** in `artifacts/e2e-build-guard/`, each with a 23 s background e2e run going:
  - main's build steps rewrote `out/main/index.js` partway through the run;
  - on this branch, `pnpm build` and `pnpm test:e2e <spec>` were both refused, `out/` kept its time and the run passed 36/36;
  - once the run had finished, `pnpm build` succeeded.
- **New integration case.** It holds a real fixture Playwright run open. The guard refuses while the run is held and allows after it exits, including with a planted finished run whose pid belongs to a live, later process. This case caught a NaN bug in my first parser.
- **New in-memory unit cases** cover the same live, finished and reused-pid judgments.
- **Local gate.** Typecheck, check and adherence pass, and the 5 affected test files pass (12 tests).
- **E2E.** Specs from all three lanes passed: ui-kit-panel, first-launch, and phase0-guardrails with answer-task.
- **Checks.** linux-checks passed on 533b86e, and main has not moved.

Risk
Low. Only `pnpm build` gains a check, and it refuses only while a run of the same working copy is provably going.

Not done
- package:mac, dist:mac, `pnpm dev` and `pnpm start` also write `out/`, but they call electron-vite directly and are not guarded.
- An e2e run started during a build's few seconds is not guarded either.
- I filed no follow-ups for these.

On the origin: FI3-346's account held up. Its tidy-up judged a run live from a live pid alone; that would have let a reused pid block builds, so the shared check now also compares start times.

tasks.outcome:
The card is up (card-da5a8392-fm-alpha-switch-steps), with commands you can copy and three figures.

You can't install the alpha straight over stable. Each cask declares conflicts_with the other, so a direct alpha install is refused and nothing changes. The steps are `brew update`, then `brew uninstall --cask firstmate-3000`, then `brew install --cask kunchenguid/tap/firstmate-3000@alpha`.

A plain uninstall only quits and removes the app. These all stay in ~/Library/Application Support/firstmate-3000 and come through untouched:
- projects, tasks, cards and settings (firstmate.db)
- crew working copies
- provider and GitHub sign-ins

tasks.outcome:
Intent
I profiled the unit suite's remaining time, focusing on the real Claude client and supervisor tests, independently of FI3-306's earlier probes. The goal was a few changes that cut full-suite time substantially, with no gate weakened, nothing skipped, and no integration coverage removed. The captain's words: "hmmm then this is not ready yet. you need to keep optimizing".

What changed
Nothing ships. This answer covers four ranked changes, and card card-443020ec-speed-answer asks the captain about the two that amend A1.

Baseline: the CI pnpm test step at 73b2a1df took 284 s (linux-checks run 36843957710). The hosted candidate median is 300.15 s. The Mac full suite is 68–71 s.

1. Run in-memory tests two at a time on CI. No decision needed.
- Change: in vitest.config.ts, give the pure and unit projects maxWorkers: Math.max(2, os.availableParallelism() - 1). The Mac stays at 9.
- Why: the hosted runner has 2 CPUs. Vitest 4.1.10's default is max(cpus−1, 1) = 1 (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.BK8pd4xc.js, resolveMaxWorkers). All 10 hosted reports in artifact 11154753193 (run 36843956431) show at most one pure/unit file at a time.
- That phase takes 132.4–135.4 s, of which 40.7–41.4 s is testing and 91.5–94.0 s is per-file startup and imports.
- Expected saving: about 45–55 s on CI (estimate).

2. Let most unit files share loaded code. Amends A1, so it needs the captain's yes.
- Change: isolate:false plus tests/helpers/pureProject.ts for most files. About 25–30 files that mock modules, stub globals or write the environment stay isolated.
- Expected saving: about 35–40 s more on CI (estimate) and about 4 s on the Mac. Changes 1 and 2 together: CI about 300 → 205–215 s.
- Prerequisite: fix the process.env writes the guard catches (NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath and PI_OFFLINE).
- Fallback if declined: pool:'threads', about 10 s on CI.

3. Write the boxed Claude launcher and Keychain shim once, keeping per-test state under each test's HOME. No decision needed.
- Expected saving: about 8.5 s on the Mac (measured). Nothing on CI.
- To cover the seat tests too, pass the API address and shim log path through HOME or env instead of baking them into the launcher (tests/e2e/mockClaudeClient.ts).

4. Run eight integration workers on the Mac instead of four. Amends A1, so it needs the captain's yes.
- Expected saving: about 13 s more on the Mac (measured). Nothing on CI.
- The Mac integration phase is limited by the worker cap: 60 s, with 3.4 of 10 cores busy.
- On CI, only a 4-vCPU runner or two shards would help. Both cost money and I did not measure them.

Verified
All runs were on the Mac at PR head 73b2a1df, each in a fresh /tmp HOME and TMPDIR. Every comparison alternated with its control.
- One versus two pure/unit workers: 47.1 s and 52.8 CPU-seconds became 24.5 s and 55.5 CPU-seconds; all 3,396 passed.
- Threads: 42.2 s alone, 22.0 s at two workers, 8.9 s versus 11.1 s at nine workers; all passed.
- Isolation off everywhere: 19.9 s, but 47 failures in 10 files, so it is not viable.
- Shared-code split: 22.6–25.1 s serial. At two workers 13.6 s and 26.8 CPU-seconds. At nine workers 6.8–6.9 s versus 10.8–11.2 s. The only failures were the guard catching environment writes.
- Real-client tracing: each test spends about 200 ms on the --version run of a freshly written launcher. The first client start takes 0.445 s versus 0.208 s for a second start in the same HOME, at the same CPU cost (0.30 versus 0.28 CPU-seconds). A probe showed a fresh script's first exec takes 95–207 ms, then 5 ms. 93 client processes use 32 of the integration cohort's 153 CPU-seconds.
- Launcher reuse (lab patch): contract file 30.4/30.5 s became 14.6/14.3 s. Classifier file 10.7/10.8 s became 7.2/7.2 s. Integration cohort over 3 pairs: 59.2/58.3/58.6 s became 49.9/50.2/50.1 s.
- Eight integration workers: 60.7 s became 47.4 s.
- Changes 3 and 4 on the full suite, 2 pairs: 68.1/67.9 s became 44.8/44.7 s, with identical 4,549 passed and 9 skipped.
- Hosted margin: the slowest CPU-bound unit test is 0.57 s, plus one deliberate 2 s wait, against the 5 s limit.
- To reproduce the hosted timeline:
  - Use the ZIP in FI3-306's working copy, .firstmate-artifacts/run-36843956431/artifact-11154753193.zip.
  - Take each testResults startTime/endTime.
  - Classify a file as integration if it is in biome.json's unit-cohort "!" exclusions, pure if under src/shared, unit otherwise.
  - Take the maximum overlap per cohort.

Risk
Low for changes 1 and 3: they change scheduling and fixture reuse only.
Medium for change 2 (order coupling between files, guarded) and change 4 (more load on the shared Mac).

Not done
- No hosted run of changes 1 or 2. Their CI numbers are estimates for the next step to confirm with PR #504's five-pair experiment.
- No measurement of a larger runner or sharding.
- Nothing committed or pushed. Instrumentation is reverted, my /tmp files are removed, and the worktree is clean.
- Card card-443020ec-speed-answer awaits the captain's choices on changes 2 and 4.

- Before: up to six crew used the ring. It places each crewmate at i/n × 360° every frame, so every join or leave re-spaces everyone.
- Now: every roster uses the planes. openPlaneSlot() gives a newcomer the midpoint of the widest gap, and survivors keep their slot. leave() and fillPlaneVacancies() never re-space.
- Only boot (settleBootRoster) or growth from zero spaces crew evenly.

Verified (established)
1. Lab vitest through the production applyCrewEvent path on an adaptive CrewOrbit, the model crewOrbit() builds. It asserts every gap is 360/n.
   - Six one-by-one arrivals on main 44865e92: 45,45,45,45,90,90 (fail).
   - At 3e19d579: the same results (fail).
   - At its parent bf59ad99: 60 × 6 (pass).
   - Seven arrivals with one finishing: 45 × 5 and 135 on main, 60 × 6 on the parent.
   - Churn (two finish, two new): 67.5,67.5,45,45,45,90 on main, 60 × 6 on the parent.
   - Boot with six: 60 × 6 on both.
2. Lab Playwright spec on the built app, with a throwaway profile and the mock provider. It sent the spawn prompt six times.
   - Main measured 90,90,45,45,45,45 from the painted label positions: a lone crewmate at the bottom with wide gaps lower-left and lower-right.
   - A restart of the same profile measured 60 × 6.
   - The bf59ad99 build was visibly even.
3. Every existing spacing check seeds crew through boot, which hides the problem.

Inferred
I did not see the captain's screenshot. A lone crewmate flanked by two 90° gaps is the shape six one-by-one arrivals always produce, so it matches the description, but the exact gaps depend on the history of joins and leaves. The stable-slot rule came from the crowded-planes study (437efc11) and then applied only above six crew. The captain's FI3-196 approval ("rather than making everyone reshuffle") was about which orbit crew sit on, not spacing within an orbit.

Risk
Low. This was read-only and nothing was committed or pushed.

Not done
No fix. The card offers three choices:
- Re-space every orbit evenly on each join and leave (default): glide that orbit's crew back to even spacing, keeping fill order and the inward glide.
- Re-space only while one orbit shows.
- Keep it as it is.
The card's details carry the fix sketch and the reproduction commands. No follow-up was filed; no existing task covers this.

tasks.outcome:
Plan round 1 for "reply sends the card to the back of the stack; a lone card stays put". The captain's card (card-fef0ce55-reply-to-back-plan) asks three questions, each with a proposed answer. The spec below records those proposed answers. Nothing is committed.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY (evidence)
- Renderer: `sendReply` (src/renderer/src/app/store.ts ~L1046) marks the card `awaiting: "answer"` before the IPC call. `visibleCards` (store.ts L84) keeps only cards where `onStage` is true (src/shared/cards.ts L232: `awaiting === undefined`), so the card leaves the stack. `reconcileStack` (store.ts ~L190) then keeps the shown card by id, or clamps the old index. Result: the card after it comes up, or the one before it if it was last. A refused reply restores the card.
- Core: `CardService.addMessage` (src/core/orchestrator/cardService.ts ~L1020) writes the `answer` hold on a captain line (`writeHold`) and drops any staged version (`applyHold`). An author line moves the hold to `close-out`. `closeOut`/`release` clear it at the crewmate's report or idle, or at the Firstmate's turn end. The hold is stored in `cards.awaiting` (migration 52), so it survives a restart.
- Stack order is `snapshot()` (cardService.ts L450): priority descending, then newest first. Host cards are 40, host notes 25, decisions 30, notes 15.
- The return is an arrival: the card comes back unread, with the pager dot and "N new". `CardNotifier` (src/core/notifications.ts) shows the native notice because the card re-enters `onStage`.
- Other readers of the hold that must keep working:
  - whose-turn and the idle ladder, through `CardStore.awaitingAuthor` (the `answer` hold only)
  - "waiting on you", through `isReadyDecision` (docs/task-record.md "Ready waiting")
  - `CrewSupervisor.act`, which refuses a click on any card with `awaiting` (crewSupervisor.ts ~L5527)
- Contract text that would go stale:
  - `CARD_REPLY` (src/core/prompts/cardContract.ts L97): "His reply takes the card off his screen, and it comes back only when you are done"
  - `THREAD_STEER_PREAMBLE` (src/core/orchestrator/wakes.ts L59): "The captain sees your card again when you report"
- Reproduction: `pnpm test src/renderer/src/app/store.test.ts src/core/orchestrator/cardService.test.ts` passes 88/88 today. That includes "hides a card the moment a reply is sent and restores it when the reply is refused" and "keeps a card the captain replied under off the stage across a restart". In e2e, `tests/e2e/card-threads.spec.ts` pins the hide in two places:
  - "a captain reply revises the card in place, or is answered in the thread" uses `watchCardLeaves` and expects the card to leave.
  - "an acknowledgement does not bring the card back, nor does a reload; the report does" expects `[data-card-layer]` count 0 while waiting.

SPEC (the card's proposed answers marked Q1–Q3)
1. A reply with two or more entries on the stack: the card moves to the back, behind every entry not waiting on its author. The shown index stays put, so the entry that followed it comes up. If the card was already last, the one before it comes up, as when a card leaves today (Q1; alternative: wrap round to the first entry).
2. A reply with exactly one entry: nothing moves and the card stays shown. The thread column opens beside it with his message and the author's working row, as the thread does today.
3. While it waits, the card stays on the stack:
   - It shows the version that was on screen at the reply until its author closes out (the existing one-rule for a card on the stage; revisions held as `staged`).
   - Thread messages paint live.
   - Cards that arrive later sort in front of it. Several sent-back cards keep reply order.
   - It stays at the back across reload and restart (held in the core).
   - Replying again sends it to the back again.
   - A waiting note never collapses into its task record.
4. Author close-out (crewmate report or idle, Firstmate turn end; restart releases `close-out` as today):
   - The card leaves the back and returns to its usual place by priority and newest (Q2; alternative: it stays at the back).
   - It redraws with the author's newest version.
   - It is marked unread unless it is the shown card, and never replaces the shown card.
   - The native notice fires when the window is unfocused, as today. `card_raised` with `returned` is recorded as today.
5. Buttons on a waiting card stay live; a click resolves against the shown version (Q3; alternative: refused until close-out, as today). The risk of live buttons: the captain can merge before the author has acted on his reply. After a closing click, an author revision under the same id could reopen the card. The author's instructions already govern that; the build step should name it under Risk.
6. Unchanged:
   - whose-turn, the idle ladder, and "waiting on you" (a waiting card is still not a ready decision)
   - the feed line `You asked crewmate N under "<title>"`
   - the thread steer and its delivery
   - a refused reply: nothing moves and the draft is kept
   - new crewmate cards still appear only at their author's close-out
   - the keeps-open Working chip
   - host agent-down cards (no reply row)
   - Firstmate cards follow the same rule as crewmate cards

ASSUMPTIONS (listed on the card)
- Applies to both Firstmate and crewmate cards.
- "One card" counts every entry the pager steps through, so an open task record counts.
- Items 3, 4 and 6 above.

DONE LOOKS LIKE (checkable)
- store.test.ts:
  - Stack [A,B,C] showing A: a sent reply leaves A at index 2 and shows B at index 0.
  - Showing C: B comes up (or A under the wrap alternative).
  - [A] alone: A stays shown at index 0 and never leaves `visibleStack` (no lostCard, no replayed entrance).
  - A refused reply changes no order.
  - An answered return marks the card unread unless it is shown.
  - A seen waiting note older than NOTE_COLLAPSE_MS does not collapse.
- cardService.test.ts:
  - After a captain message, `snapshot()` keeps the card present and visible, after the cards not waiting and after earlier sent-back cards.
  - A crewmate revision during the wait leaves the shown version until `closeOut`.
  - After `closeOut` the card is back in priority/newest order (or still last under Q2's alternative).
  - A new CardService over the same store keeps the hold and the order.
  - `awaitingAuthor` and `threadAwaitingAuthor` are unchanged.
- notifications.test.ts: an answered return notifies when unfocused.
- crewSupervisor.test.ts: `act` on a waiting card resolves (Q3 yes) or refuses (Q3 no).
- e2e card-threads.spec.ts:
  - Rewrite the first test: the lone card stays on the stage with the thread beside it.
  - Reshape the acknowledgement test: with two cards, a reply brings up the other card at "1 / 2", and the replied card sits at "2 / 2" with no new dot. The acknowledgement does not redraw it. A reload keeps the order. The report redraws it with the answer, returns it to its place, and the pager shows "1 new".
  - Re-run "ready waiting follows reachable choices through Working, reply, reload and return".
- Contract and docs:
  - Reword `CARD_REPLY` and `THREAD_STEER_PREAMBLE` to: his reply sends the card to the back of his stack (a lone card stays), and he sees your answer only when you are done.
  - Bump `FIRSTMATE_CONTRACT_VERSION` with a note in contractVersion.ts; piResources.test.ts must pass; run `pnpm replay:gate`.
  - Update docs/card-threads.md ("When a card reaches the stage", "A reply does hand the turn…", the moved-notes paragraph), CardStack.prompt.md and CardThread.prompt.md in the design skill, and the "off the stage" comments in cardService, store, notifications and crewSupervisor.
- Gate: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence`, the unit files above, and card-threads.spec.ts alone with `--no-deps`.

SUGGESTED MECHANISM
- In the core, persist a "sent back at" stamp on the `cards` row (new migration), so the order survives a restart.
- `writeHold("answer")` stamps it and keeps the shown version staged instead of dropping it.
- `snapshot()` sorts stamped cards last, oldest stamp first. `release`/`closeOut` clear the stamp (kept under Q2's alternative).
- `onStage` hides only a card waiting for its first close-out: true when not awaiting, or when stamped.
- In the renderer:
  - `sendReply` stops forcing the hide and sets the shown index per item 1.
  - `applyCards` stops its `sendingReplies` override.
  - `reconcileStack` counts a cleared stamp as an arrival and excludes waiting cards from `aged`.
- `act` admits a stamped card (Q3 yes). The notifier treats a stamped→answered change as becoming ready.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Cyclic paging.
- Any new animation for the move.
- When new cards first appear.
- Working, close, dismiss and the reply composer.
- The whose-turn sort and the idle ladder.
- Observe's UI.

tasks.outcome:
Answer, on card fi3-395-no-checks-reads-passed: the app's one check rule (forge.ts overallOfChecks) reads an empty list of checks as passed. That rule is meant for projects with no CI. But this project runs linux-checks only on pull_request events, so every new pull request, and every push to one, has no checks for a few seconds to over a minute. In that gap the crewmate's check_change, the completion card's last check (pendingCiGate), Firstmate's check_pr_ci and the merge click all read green. The crewmate instructions (piResources.ts:45 and :51, forgeTools.ts:32) also say that no checks means the local gate is the evidence.

Established from the record, which corrects the brief:
- PR #549's card never reached the captain. check_change read "green, no checks" 2s after the pull request opened. emit_card at 10:16:05 was refused at 10:16:06, because linux-checks had queued by then. The crewmate's report still said "Completion card emitted", and no crewmate card exists for FI3-387.
- No code takes a shown card down when its checks start.
- The card that vanished at 10:19 was FI3-306's PR #504 card, which was green. Merge was chosen on it at 10:13, while its crewmate was mid-turn. The crewmate re-emitted it at 10:19:14, and the merge ran at 10:19:24.
- Premature cards did reach the captain twice before. PR #338 (FI3-64, September 25) and PR #496 (FI3-292, September 30) each went up on a no-checks green. In both, the Merge click found checks running and was refused, and the card vanished. #338's checks then failed.
- 74 crewmate sessions on this project got a no-checks "green", and 11 of those were then refused by the card's last check.
- FI3-387 is stuck right now. Its fix version 516d1e58 needs bringing up to date with main, which conflicted from 4224ad44 at 10:23. GitHub runs no pull_request workflows on a conflicting pull request, and no run existed at 10:32. Its recorded CI is "green" and no watch is set, so the wake its crewmate is waiting for will not come. It needs a steer to bring PR #549 up to date.

Inferred: the first-seconds gap is GitHub's queue.

Could not find out: whether GitHub's branch protection would refuse a merge clicked inside the gap, which would otherwise merge unchecked work.

Proposed default ("File the fix"): on GitHub, no checks reads "waiting for checks to start" whenever GitHub already has a workflow run for that version or the project's earlier pull requests reported checks. That reading arms the check watch, and GitHub's not-mergeable state is named. All four readers change together, and the instruction lines and docs are reworded. The alternatives on the card are instructions only, or leaving it as it is.

Filed FI3-401: a refused completion card should reach Firstmate as a typed fact, so a false "emitted" report is not relayed.

How I got this: I read the code and ran the two pinned zero-checks tests (both pass). I read a scratch copy of the app's database, the crewmate session files and GitHub's run list. Nothing was committed or pushed.

tasks.outcome:
Outcome: the captain's reply is folded into the plan and the card (card-be3e325a-fi3-398-slow-stage-hover-summary-plan, now titled "Plan: slow the stage near the pointer, pause on a crewmate, and summarize it") is revised in place. His words, verbatim: "when mouse actually hover on a crewmate, let's pause the animation completely. also, avoid text wrapping in the small popover if possible. we can ellipsis". That decides the speed profile (the old question 1 is gone) and the summary's line rule. One new question follows from "completely": whether the character's eyes stay alive during the pause. Eight questions remain on the card, each with my proposed answer; his other picks were all still "as proposed" when he replied, which is context and not yet his choice. Nothing was committed, pushed or opened. This report supersedes the earlier one in full.

== How it stands today (evidence, unchanged) ==
- Two independent animation loops through useAnimationLoop (src/renderer/src/character/motion.ts:12), each handed the raw frame time: the character at src/renderer/src/character/Firstmate.tsx:1510 and the crew at src/renderer/src/character/crew/CrewOrbit.tsx:116. Nothing shares or scales time.
- The crew model is time-injected and DOM-free (character/crew/orbit.ts): travel is absolute in `now` (orbitalPlanes.ts planePhase; +8/-20/-4 deg/s at radii 164/210/256 px), clips are `now - stampedAt`. The character's machine (character/machine.ts) is time-injected; drawFrame mixes dt-integrated motion (rotation, gaze, blink) with `now`-based terms (breath, flicker, notice, send-off).
- Stamps come from performance.now() at app/store.ts:579 (seedCrew), app/store.ts:1268 (applyCrewEvent), crew/crewSignal.ts:25 (constructor), Firstmate.tsx:619 (createSim) and Firstmate.tsx:1456 (tap).
- Crewmates are not hoverable: both crew canvases and the formation root are pointer-events none (CrewOrbit.tsx:207-232). The only inspection is the model-name label button (CrewOrbit.tsx:253-291, crew/modelLabels.css): hover, focus or click shows the full name in a plate under the formation; labels exist only while one orbit is occupied (crew/modelLabels.ts) and the Settings switch is on; the documented rule is "inspecting never pauses or changes the animation" (docs/crew-orbits.md "Model-name labels"; design skill components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md and readme "Crewmates").
- The pointer already feeds the gaze from a window-level pointermove listener (Firstmate.tsx:1464-1508); the gaze lets go of a resting pointer after 2.5 s (character/face.ts DEFAULT_POINTER_GAZE.holdSeconds).
- Data: the task board subscription behind the name labels (crew/useCrewModelNames.ts, read "tasks.board") carries key, title, workPosture and model (src/shared/tasks.ts taskViewSchema); workPostureLabel (src/shared/workPosture.ts) gives the Tasks dot's state words; the one-task read "tasks.detail" (src/shared/reads.ts:219) carries activityLog, the record's condensed Activity (src/core/tasks/recordActivity.ts), invalidated live by that task's events; openRecord(taskId) exists in the shell store (app/store.ts:1123).
- Geometry: at 1200x800 the stage centre is 312 px above the input's top edge and the outer orbit plus 40 px is 296 px, so the zone never reaches the input; the formation's fit scale keeps that at the 640 px minimum height.

== Spec (DECIDED items marked; the rest are my defaults pending questions 1-8) ==
Part 1 - slow, then pause
1. One shared stage clock (new DOM-free, time-injected module beside character/motion.ts; a module ref like liveVoiceLevel, never store state). Stage time advances by real dt times a rate; both loops and every stamp listed above read stage time, so the character's turning, crew travel and spin, spawns, departures, packets, nudges, flickers and emotes slow and stop together. At rate 1 stage time equals real time, so resting behaviour is unchanged.
2. DECIDED (captain): three levels. Rate 1 outside the zone; SLOW inside it; 0 - a complete pause - while the pointer is on a crewmate. Zone = a circle round the character's centre with radius of the outermost occupied orbit (164, 210 or 256 px times the formation's fit scale) plus 40 px. The "graded" and "keep drifting" directions are dropped.
3. The pause begins the moment the hit test acquires a crewmate (not after the summary's dwell), so the target does not slide away; it ends when the pointer leaves that crewmate's release radius, Esc is pressed, the frame hides under a card, or the crewmate itself is gone, returning to SLOW if the pointer is still in the zone.
4. SLOW = 0.10 [Q1; alternatives 0.05, 0.20]. At 0.10 the middle orbit moves about 7 px/s.
5. Easing: every drop (to SLOW, to 0) with a ~0.11 s time constant (settled in about a third of a second), every rise with ~0.23 s (about 0.7 s). Never a cut.
6. Resting pointer [Q2 default "lets go"]: when the pointer is inside the zone, not on a crewmate, and has not moved for 3 s, the target returns to 1; the next move slows again. A pointer resting on a crewmate holds the pause indefinitely. [Alternative: stays slow while inside.]
7. No crew out [Q3 default]: no slowdown. [Alternative: slows anyway.]
8. Eyes [Q4, NEW, default "alive"]: during the pause every structure stops but the eyes keep blinking and following the pointer on real time. [Alternative: the eyes freeze with the stage.] Assumed regardless: while only slowed, the eyes run on real time.
9. Rate target is 1 whenever the pointer is outside the window, the window is blurred or hidden, the character frame is hidden under a card or record (HomeMate's showCards / inert), or the view is not home. Theme re-read timers (Firstmate.tsx:785, CrewOrbit.tsx:180) stay on real time. Reduced motion is unchanged (one settled frame; no rate concept).

Part 2 - the hover summary
10. Hover is a hit test in formation coordinates against the frames orbit.update already returns (a pure, unit-tested function in crew/), run on pointer moves: acquire within max(glyph/2 + 8, 18) px of a painted centre, nearest wins and the nearer-to-camera one on a tie; release beyond 1.6x that radius. Acquisition needs pointer movement: a crewmate drifting under a still pointer triggers neither the pause nor the summary. Works at every crew size and on all three orbits, independent of the model-name switch.
11. One summary element (DOM, not canvas), shown ~120-140 ms after acquisition, placed beside the crewmate on the side away from the character, flipped or clamped to stay inside the window and clear of the input and rails, joined to the crewmate by a hairline, the crewmate ringed [Q6 default "quiet"; alternative "instrument" = corner brackets, squarer corners, an uppercase micro label over each line]. Since the stage is paused it is positioned once per hover. Counter-scaled so its type stays at size when the formation is fitted to a short window. Look: --bg-2 solid, hairline border, --radius-m, no glow; fade in over --dur-fast with a 4 px drift; close is a cut.
12. DECIDED (captain): nothing in the summary wraps. Each fact is one line; the panel is as wide as its longest line up to a fixed maximum (about 240 px), and a longer title, state or note ends in an ellipsis. The note's age stays visible at the line's end (the note text is what truncates). Assumed: a cut-short line is not expanded in place; the record a click opens has the full text.
13. Content [Q5 default "both"]: line 1 task key (mono, --fg-3) + state dot (ember when the posture is active, cyan otherwise) + workPostureLabel words; line 2 the task title (--fg-1); line 3 the newest row of the record's condensed Activity (tasks.detail activityLog last row) + its age in mono; line 4 the full model display name. [Alternatives: state only, or note only.] Key, title, state and model paint at once from the board; the note fills in when the one-task read answers and stays live while open, pause or not. No live tool names or streaming text.
14. Click [Q7 default yes]: a click on the hovered crewmate calls openRecord(taskId). No other action; the summary has no buttons.
15. Name plate [Q8 default "fold in"]: the bottom full-name plate (.fm-crew-model-full-name) is removed; the short name labels stay, and hovering or focusing a label opens the same summary and pause for that crewmate (the keyboard path where labels exist; beyond one orbit the Tasks panel remains the keyboard route - assumed). [Alternative: keep the plate.]
16. Reduced motion: the summary works against the still frame (hit test on pointer events, since the loop is not running).

== What done looks like (checkable) ==
- Pointer absent or outside the zone: stage rate is 1 and the existing specs pass unchanged (tests/e2e crew-orbit, crew-planes, crew-tiers, crew-review-electrons, token-flicker, character-*; machine, orbit and orbitalPlanes unit tests unchanged in meaning).
- Unit: the stage clock integrates rate x dt, eases with the stated constants, is idempotent per frame time when two loops ask, holds stage time constant at rate 0, and returns to 1 on leave/blur/hidden; the hit test acquires, sticks and releases at the stated radii and prefers the nearer crewmate.
- E2E (new spec, e.g. tests/e2e/crew-hover.spec.ts; hermetic launch, rows via seedTask): pointer into the zone -> the published stage rate (a data attribute on the near canvas, like data-formation) reaches SLOW and a crewmate's travel per frame drops while its travel per unit of stage time is unchanged (order/work, no wall-clock window). Pointer onto a crewmate -> the rate reaches 0 and that crewmate's painted position is identical across later frames; an event arriving during the pause (a spawn or report) shows no motion until the pointer leaves, then plays. Leaving the crewmate returns to SLOW, leaving the zone, blurring or opening a record returns to 1; with no crew the rate stays 1. The summary shows that task's key, title, workPostureLabel text, the record's newest Activity row and model name, at 1, 9 and 21 crew; every line is exactly one line high, and a seeded long title and long note are truncated with an ellipsis while the panel's width stays at its maximum; Esc and leaving close it; a click opens the record card for that task id; under a shown card nothing opens; with reduced motion the summary still opens. Both themes and the minimum window: the summary stays inside the window at unscaled type.
- A resting frame with no hover performs no DOM writes beyond today's.
- Docs updated in the same change: docs/crew-orbits.md (new section; the "without stopping the orbit" sentence and the full-name plate paragraph revised), docs/renderer.md character notes (the stage clock as the one time source), the design skill's components/mate/Crewmate.prompt.md and readme "Crewmates" (the rule "inspecting never pauses or changes the animation" replaced by the captain's new rule - skill first, then code, per AGENTS.md), and tests/e2e/crew-model-labels.spec.ts:145-152 (full-name plate assertions) moved to the summary.

== Left alone ==
Orbit geometry, speeds, capacities and re-spacing (orbitalPlanes.ts, FI3-340), tier solids, review electrons, the token-flicker mapping, the character's machine states and captain-verified behaviours, label visibility rules and the Settings switch, the Tasks panel, the task record, and the whole core: no wire, IPC, storage or schema change.

== Out of scope ==
Acting on a crewmate from the summary (steer, stop, merge - writes still go through Firstmate), a summary for the Firstmate itself, live tool or streaming detail, a settings toggle, expanding truncated text in place, touch gestures, changes to the Crew strip or feed.

== Risks and notes for the build ==
- During a pause the painted scene is stale by design: a crewmate that turns idle, reports or leaves while the pointer rests on another shows it only on resume (its colour blend and clips ride stage time). The summary's words are DOM and stay current. If the hovered crewmate's own task closes during the pause, the summary closes and the stage resumes.
- While slowed, clips stretch: at 10% a spawn spark takes ~7 s and a token flicker ~20 s; events are stamped in stage time, so order is preserved. The machine's submit-anticipation grace window stretches too, and stops in a pause; if that reads wrong, keep that one timer on real time.
- Typing or talking does not cancel the slowdown or the pause by itself; a pointer parked on a crewmate while the captain types keeps the stage paused. Question 2's release covers only the parked-in-zone case. If listening should restore full speed, that is a one-line target rule - not asked yet.
- FI3-396 (even re-spacing, orbit.ts) and FI3-400 (empty label when unassigned, useCrewModelNames.ts / CrewOrbit.tsx) are live and touch the same files; the build brings itself up to date with them first. The implementation task is FI3-399 (basis: this task).

== Verification of the revised card ==
Rendered in headless Chromium against the app's token and frame stylesheets (dark and light at the usual 510 px column, dark at the 350 px narrow column) and exercised: 100% idle, 10% in the zone, release after 3 s still, 0% on a crewmate and still 0% with the summary unmoved after 4 s, every summary line one line high (15/18/18/15 px) with the long note ellipsized at the 240 px cap, 100% after leaving, 5% with the twentieth pick, state-only and instrument variants, no script errors in any run.

## Intent
Build the accepted FI3-398 plan with the captain's picks: a tenth of normal speed inside the formation, a complete pause on a crewmate, release after about 3 s still unless resting on a crewmate, no slow-down with an empty orbit, eyes that still blink and follow during the pause, a summary with state now and latest note in the instrument look, nothing wrapping, a click that opens the record, and the model plate folded into the summary.

## What changed
- One shared stage clock (`src/renderer/src/character/stageClock.ts`) is now the time source for both animation loops and every stamp the stage animates, so the character and crew slow and stop together. At rate 1 it is bit-identical to the frame time.
- `crew/CrewOrbit.tsx` watches the pointer and sets the rate: 1 away from the formation, 0.1 inside the zone (outermost occupied orbit plus 40 px), 0 on a crewmate, eased down in about a third of a second and up in about 0.7 s.
- The character's eyes run on real time, so they keep blinking and following through a pause.
- Pointing is a pure hit test (`crew/hover.ts`) run on pointer movement only; Esc lets go; a click calls `openRecord`.
- The summary (`crew/CrewSummary.tsx`) shows key and state, title, the newest Activity row with its age, and the full model name, one line each up to 240 px with an ellipsis, with corner brackets and a hairline.
- The full-name plate is removed; pointing at or focusing a name opens the same summary and pause. `useCrewModelNames` became `useCrewBoard`.
- Docs and the design skill are updated (`docs/crew-orbits.md`, `docs/renderer.md`, `Crewmate.prompt.md`, the readme's Crewmates bullet).
- No core, wire, IPC, storage or schema change.

## Verified
- Pull request #557 at 81953b2: `linux-checks` completed with success, read with check_change immediately before the card.
- Local gate on that commit: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm check && pnpm lint:adherence` with 0 errors, `pnpm exec vitest run --project pure --project unit` (293 files, 3,441 tests), `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/crew-hover.spec.ts --project=desktop`: 6 passed against the real hidden app.
  - The published rate is 1 outside the zone, 0.1 inside (a crewmate's measured speed was between 0.05 and 0.2 of full speed) and 0 on a crewmate.
  - A resting pointer inside the zone releases to 1, and the next move slows the stage again.
  - Over 4.5 s paused, the crew canvases stayed pixel-identical with no DOM writes, the character's structure did not change, and its eyes did.
  - A crewmate commissioned during the pause appeared only after the pointer left.
  - Esc, leaving the crewmate, leaving the zone and a window blur each behave as planned; a click opens the right record and nothing opens under it.
  - With no crew the rate stays 1.
  - At 1, 9 and 21 crew the summary's rows are one line high, cut with an ellipsis at the 240 px maximum, at unscaled type and inside the window; at 21 crew this also holds in both themes, at the minimum window and under reduced motion.
- Existing specs pass unchanged: crew-model-labels (plate assertions moved to the summary), crew-planes, crew-tiers, crew-review-electrons, token-flicker, task-record-stack, reply-emotes, phase1-shell, crew-orbit, character-gaze, character-blackhole, character-sky-fidgets, first-turn-label, stack-visibility.
- Six screenshots from those runs are on the completion card; none are committed.

Medium: every home-stage animation now reads the stage clock, though at rate 1 it equals the frame time exactly and the existing character and crew specs pass unchanged.

## Not done
Where the plan turned out wrong or was adjusted:
- "Clear of the rails" could not mean the whole rail columns. With both rails docked the open stage is 600 px wide at the default window, so nearly every summary would have flipped onto the character. The summary instead avoids the rails' actual panels, the top bar and the input, and goes under or over the crewmate before the character's side.
- The plan's geometry note, that the zone never reaches other surfaces, misses that the rail columns take the pointer. A crewmate passing under a rail column cannot be pointed at there.
- "Returning to SLOW" after Esc does not hold for a pointer that has rested more than 3 s. The resting rule sends the stage to full speed until the next move.
- The test fixture's `createdAt: Date.now() + i` put each record's creation after its own events. The shared roster fixture now creates rows in the past.

Other notes:
- One early local run of a new test, before I removed the fixture account, let the Firstmate's turn reach OpenRouter with the fixture key and got a 401. The test now deletes that account as crew-model-labels does.
- The new spec sits in the default serial desktop lane.
- Out of scope as planned: actions from the summary, a summary for the Firstmate, live tool detail, a settings toggle, expanding cut text in place, touch gestures, a keyboard path to crew beyond one orbit.
- The full e2e suite and `pnpm package:mac` were not run.

No follow-ups filed.
